It is significant as the site of a chimpanzee reintroduction project, and it also contains riparian forest and animals such as Guinea baboons, green monkeys, western red colobus, warthogs, and hippopotamuses."}

{"digest":"Yundum is a city in The Gambia, south of Banjul and beside the international airport. It has two parts, Yundum and Old Yundum. The passage links it with Abuko Nature Reserve, a small protected area outside Lamin that gives a good introduction to Gambian wildlife. Visitors can see monkeys, crocodiles, about 300 bird species, bushbucks, and chameleons. The reserve is noted as one of the smallest protected areas in Africa."}

{"digest":"Badou is a town of about 24,000 people in the Akposso mountains and the capital and main market of Wawa district, a border area known for cocoa production. Visitors can see a busy market town where agriculture dominates daily life, especially at harvest time in early November, when farmers bring in products and trucks carry coffee and cocoa toward Lomé for export. Near Badou, Akloa Falls is reached by a 40-minute hike through cocoa plantations and forest to a 100-metre waterfall. The Ghana border is about 10 km away."}

{"digest":"Okeluse Forest Reserve is a major forest reserve in Okeluse, an agrarian community in Ose Local Government Area of Ondo State, Nigeria. It covers 144 square kilometres and sits at about 68 metres above sea level. The passage describes it as a forest habitat that supports sustainable wood production and provides economic, social, and environmental benefits. It also notes that human activities, including agriculture, urbanization, and deforestation, are degrading the forest and threatening species such as chimpanzees."}

{"digest":"Ilhéu de Baluarte is a small, uninhabited islet in Cape Verde, about 2 km off the northeastern coast of Boa Vista. It is the easternmost land mass in the country and forms part of the protected Reserva Natural Integral Ilhéu de Baluarte, along with the surrounding marine area. The isle is flat, rocky, and made of basaltic rocks, with its highest point under five meters. Visits are only allowed with permission from local authorities."}

{"digest":"São Filipe is the capital of Fogo island in Cape Verde, on the west coast of Africa. Visitors can explore its historic center, Bila Baxo, known for colonial architecture, renovated houses, colourful facades, wooden balconies, bay windows, and about 50 representative mansions. Notable sights include the city hall at Praça 12 de Setembro, the wooden pavilion and small park there, the church of Nossa Senhora da Conceição, the Market Hall, and the Casa da Memória museum. The center is on the tentative World Heritage list."}

{"digest":"Sawla is the capital of Sawla-Tuna-Kalba District in Ghana’s Savannah Region and a busy road junction on the Wa-Damongo-Tamale highway. Visitors mainly pass through or stay overnight here en route to Mole National Park and other towns. In town, there is a daily market, lorry station, guesthouses, fuel stations, and a linear settlement along the main road. Travellers can visit Tuna and Kalba villages for traditional architecture and shea processing, or walk the market and see savanna farms and birds."}

{"digest":"Mont Sângbé National Park is a national park in Ivory Coast, in the Monts du Toura west of the Sassandra River, north of Man between Biankouma and Touba. It covers rugged mountainous land with granitic inselbergs and peaks over 700 m. Visitors would see mostly dense savanna woodland, with small patches of deciduous forest and gallery forest, plus drier Sudanian woodland in the north. It is significant for its wildlife, including western chimpanzees, elephants, buffaloes and several duiker species, and is an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Banana Islands in Sierra Leone are a tourist destination about 40 km from Freetown, used for day trips and overnight stays. Visitors can see two fishing communities, Dublin and Ricketts, and take a historical walking tour of churches, a cemetery, a school, a fort, a slaver’s house, and a fishing harbour. The passage also says the islands have rich history as the first European settlement in the region. Activities include sport fishing, scuba diving, snorkeling, guided forest walks, and historical and cultural tours."}

{"digest":"Monte Estância is a mountain in the southeastern part of Boa Vista, Cape Verde. At 387 m, it is the island’s highest point, set 4 km from the Atlantic coast and 23 km southeast of the capital, Sal Rei. It lies within a protected natural space designated as a natural monument covering 739 ha. A visitor would see the mountain itself and the surrounding protected area. The passage identifies it mainly for its status as Boa Vista’s highest point and protected natural monument."}

{"digest":"Douroula is a town in Burkina Faso and the county seat of Douroula Department in Mouhoun province. Near the town are ruins of a smelting furnace and traces of ferrous metallurgy dating to the 8th century BC. A visitor would see these ancient remains, which are described as the oldest confirmed metallurgy site in Burkina Faso. Douroula was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List with other ancient metallurgy complexes as part of the Ancient Ferrous Metallurgy Sites of Burkina Faso."}

{"digest":"Koforidua is a city in southern Ghana, in Ashanti-Kwahu, and serves as a commercial hub of the Eastern Region. Visitors would see a place with colonial and modern architecture, businesses, and heavy duty industries. The area also includes Obuo Tabri Mountain, which is considered sacred and has scenery that attracts tourists, as well as waterfalls such as Akaa Falls and Boti Falls. At Boti Falls, there are 200 underground steps and a palmnut tree with three branches in one tree."}

{"digest":"Terjit, also called Tergit, is a lush green oasis settlement in Saharan Mauritania, about 45 km south of Atar. It sits in a gorge on the western edge of the Adrar Plateau, with a palm grove stretching along a stream from a spring. Visitors can relax in the oasis, use picnic areas, and cool off in a small natural pool. Several hikes run around the oasis. The passage also notes its historical use for religious ceremonies, wedding ceremonies, and the coronation of a few African princes."}

{"digest":"Yamoussoukro is the capital of Côte d'Ivoire, laid out as a grid of paved streets and lights that now have potholes and places where jungle is reclaiming them. Visitors can see the public gardens, the Fondation Felix Houphouet-Boigny, and the old Presidential Palace, all linked to spending under Felix Houphouet-Boigny. The main sight is the Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, described as the largest Christian church in the world and modeled on St. Peter's Basilica. A nearby hospital was required at its consecration, and the cornerstone still stands alone."}

{"digest":"The Symposium de sculpture sur granit de Laongo is a sculpture site about 35 km from Ouagadougou, in Oubritenga province, founded in 1989 by Burkinabe sculptor Siriky Ky. Invited sculptors work on site, carving granite from the location itself, and some pieces combine granite with materials such as metal. The symposium began as a biennial event and first opened with 18 sculptors from 13 countries. Its legal status was unclear as of 2010."}

{"digest":"The Chief’s Palace, also called the Sandema Chief’s Palace or Abil-Yeri community, is in the centre of Sandema. It is the home of the overlord of the entire Builsa lands, Nab Azantilow Azagsug II. The passage notes that he is the son of the late Dr. Nab Ayieta Azantilow, who was known for his bravery during the World War."}

{"digest":"Idanre is a historic town in Ondo State, Nigeria, about 20 km southeast of Akure. It lies in the rainforest zone and is surrounded by inselbergs. Visitors would see the Idanre Hills, a cultural and environmental landmark with a unique ecosystem, and cultural sites such as Owa’s Palace, shrines, the Old Court, Belfry, Agbooogun footprint, thunder water (Omi Apaara), and burial mounds and grounds. The town is also a trade center and farming region, especially for cocoa."}

{"digest":"Taruga is an archaeological site in Nigeria, about 60 km southeast of Abuja in the Middle Belt. Visitors would see the evidence of the Nok culture excavated there, including terracotta figurines and pottery decorated with comb stamping, grooving, chevrons, hatched triangles, raised dots and net-like patterns. The site is significant for finds dated to around 600 BC and for evidence of very early iron working. Bernard Fagg’s excavation in the 1960s found figurines and iron slag, and Taruga holds the earliest known date for iron working in Sub-Saharan Africa."}

{"digest":"Man is a market town in the Southwestern Forests of Côte d'Ivoire and the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Man, with Saint-Michel cathedral. Visitors can see the La Dent de Man rocky outcrop overlooking the town, the waterfalls around Man, and the monkey forest. The waterfalls are set in tropical forest with dragonflies and butterflies; people swim there, and one site has a small shop and toilets. Nearby mountains, including Tonkoui and Le Dent de Man, are used for hiking and views."}

{"digest":"Natitingou is a town in northern Benin. From there, visitors can travel about 50 km to Pendjari National Park to see West African wildlife, or drive an hour or two to the falls of Tanougou and the Betammaribe’s mud castles, known as the Tata Somba. The town’s main street has a statue of Mathieu Kérékou, Benin’s longtime president. The passage also mentions the calming sight of Chutes de Kota, or waterfalls."}

{"digest":"Kirikongo is an archaeological site in the Mouhoun Bend region of Burkina Faso. Visitors would not see a modern tourist attraction but the remains of an Iron Age village spread across thirteen mounds in a 37-hectare area, with a village center and outlying clusters. The mounds represented households built of earthen materials with clay floors. The site is significant for evidence of iron smelting, ground-stone agricultural processing, and long occupation from about AD 100 to 1700, linked to the ancestors of the Bwa."}
{"skip": true}

{"digest":"Kogyae Strict Nature Reserve is a strict nature reserve near Kumasi, Ghana, established in 1971 and covering 386 km2. Visitors would see wildlife such as African buffalos, African civets, civet cats, monkeys, and 85 bird species. The reserve’s symbol is the waterbuck. The passage presents it as a protected park area in Ghana with notable animal diversity."}

{"digest":"Ténéré is a desert region in south central Sahara, stretching from northeastern Niger to western Chad. A visitor would see a vast plain of sand, with the Erg of Bilma sand dunes in the centre, and flat basin terrain that was once the bed of prehistoric Lake Chad. It lies between several mountain ranges, including the Aïr, Hoggar, Djado, and Tibesti. The passage also notes its significance as the centre of the Neolithic Tenerian culture and as one of the most extreme, hyper-arid environments on Earth."}

{"digest":"Òkè-Ìlá Òràngún is an ancient town in Osun State, southwestern Nigeria, and the present headquarters of Ifedayo Local Government Area. It was once the capital of an ancient city-state in the Igbomina area of Yorubaland and was part of the original Ìlá-Yàrà kingdom. Visitors can see Ayikunnugba Waterfalls in a cliffed gorge with caves and underground passages, Omi-Ogan Waterfalls in a valley, and Oke Lanfo Peak, which offers panoramic views of nearby towns. The town is known for the Elewe masquerade and Igbomina Yoruba traditions."}

{"digest":"Mont Agou is the highest mountain in Togo, south east of Kpalimé in the Plateaux Region, near the Ghana border. From the summit, Ghana can be seen. Visitors can also see remains of military installations near the top, including structures from the German era and French Togoland, among them a French military hospital from World War II. The mountain rises abruptly above the Danyi Plateau and is significant locally as a symbol of resistance, linked to Ewe history and to the defence of the area against Ashanti troops."}

{"digest":"Monogaga Classified Forest is a 350 km2 forest in the Sassandra and San-Pédro Departments of Côte d'Ivoire. Parts of it are managed as protected areas where exploitation is banned, while other parts are used for farming. The passage says the forest might still hold a chimpanzee population of over 100 individuals, although surveys have not observed the species there, suggesting it is very rare. Its conservation significance lies in this possible chimpanzee range."}

{"digest":"Guinness Ghana Breweries is a Ghanaian brewery founded in 1960 and based in the Kaase Industrial Area in Kumasi, with representation in Accra at the former premises of Achimota Brewery Company in Achimota, at Tata Brewery Ltd. A visitor would mainly see a brewery site linked to Ghana’s industrial history rather than a tourist attraction. The passage notes it first produced only Guinness Foreign Extra Stout and that it is listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange."}

{"digest":"Dakar is the capital and largest city of Senegal, and a cultural and commercial center of French-speaking West Africa. It lies at the end of the Cap Verte peninsula, the westernmost point of the African mainland. Visitors may use it as a first stop for exploring the region, with good flight connections to Western Europe, and can experience international events that have grown tourism, including the Dakar Rally and the Contemporary Art Biennale. The original Lebou villages of Ouakam, Ngor, Yoff and Hann remain distinct neighbourhoods today, and the city’s history includes Portuguese contact, colonial rule, and the slave trade."}

{"digest":"Assin Manso Slave River Site, also called Nnonkonsuo or Donkor Nsuo, is a historic slave market and river site in Ghana’s Central Region. It was the final link in the slavery route from Northern Ghana and the place where enslaved people had their last bath on African soil before being taken to Elmina and Cape Coast. Visitors can see the Ancestral Graveyard and Memorial Wall of Return, walk barefoot to the muddy river through a bamboo grove, place their hands in the water, and offer prayers. It gained renewed attention after a 1998 reburial ceremony."}

{"digest":"Banco National Park is a national park in central Abidjan, Ivory Coast, along Highway North in Attécoubé. It is one of the few dense, primary tropical forests in the middle of an urban area and is described as the second largest urban park in the world. Visitors would see a 600-hectare primary forest with rare trees such as mahogany and avodire, plus a hydraulic reservoir. The reservoir is important to Abidjan and feeds 29 boreholes from its water table."}

{"digest":"Comoé National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Biosphere Reserve in north-eastern Ivory Coast, in the Zanzan and Savanes districts. It is West Africa’s largest protected area, covering 11,500 square kilometres. Visitors would find a range of habitats, from humid Guinea savanna to dry Sudanian zones, including savanna types, gallery forests, riparian grasslands, rock outcrops, forest islands, and patches of tropical rainforest around the Comoé River. The park is noted for its rich biodiversity and for having been removed from the World Heritage in Danger list after conservation improvements."}

{"digest":"Gwoza is a town in Borno State in northeastern Nigeria near the border of Cameroon. Visitors can hike and explore the Mandara Mountains and the Gwoza Hills, see rock formations, caves, and panoramic views of the town, and visit the Emir's Palace, Central Mosque, local markets, Gwoza Museum, and nearby traditional villages. The passage says the mountains form a natural barrier between Nigeria and Cameroon and notes caves, historical sites, trade routes, wildlife, and birdwatching as part of the area’s significance."}

{"digest":"Fort Metal Cross, originally Fort Dixcove, is a military fort on a promontory at Infuma in Dixcove, in Ghana’s Western Region. A visitor would see a historic fort site that was used in the Atlantic slave trade, as a slave prison, and as a service station for timber supply and ship repairs. It was besieged twice in 1712, later passed between the Dutch and British, and has also served as a police station and postal station. It is part of the Forts and Castles UNESCO World Heritage Site."}

{"digest":"Bobo-Dioulasso is Burkina Faso’s second largest city and a major center of culture and music. Visitors see many historic buildings, a busy social life, and places such as Cine Sanyon and the Centre Culturel Francaise, where there may be exhibits, art, music, or a garden for reading and studying. The Grande Mosquée is a Sahel-style mud mosque built in 1832 after a local king promised to construct it in return for help against an invasion from the Kenedougou Kingdom."}

{"digest":"Western Area Peninsula National Park is a protected area in Sierra Leone, covering 183.37 km2. It was first a forest reserve in 1916 and became a national park in 2012. The park is the westernmost semi-deciduous closed canopy forest in the country and contains endangered birds and three species of duiker. Visitors can also go to the Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary, which cares for abused, orphaned and abandoned chimpanzees and educates Sierra Leoneans about protecting chimpanzees in the wild."}

{"digest":"Praia da Varandinha is a beach on the southwest coast of Boa Vista in Cape Verde, north of the headland Ponta Varandinha. It forms part of the protected Morro de Areia Nature Reserve. Nearby is Ponta Varandinha, the island’s westernmost point, where there is a lighthouse. The nearest village is Povoação Velha, about 5 km to the east. A visitor would see the beach and the headland setting within the reserve."}

{"digest":"Nimba National Forest, also called the Mount Nimba Forest Reserves, is a national forest in Nimba County, Liberia, along the borders with Guinea and Ivory Coast. It has eastern and western sections covering 96 km2 and 91 km2. Visitors would be dealing with a protected forest noted for birdlife rather than established tourist facilities. It is designated an Important Bird Area because it supports significant populations of many bird species. The passage also notes reports of western chimpanzees there before the civil wars and later damage from fighting, extraction, and displacement."}

{"digest":"Kalissaye Avifaunal Reserve is a small nature reserve in Senegal at the mouth of Kalissaye Pond in the middle of the Casamance River. It is closed because of the Casamance Conflict. The reserve was created in 1978 to protect sea turtle and seabird colonies. Visitors would see small sandy islands with coastal plants, and wildlife including Caspian terns, royal terns, great white pelicans, loggerhead and green turtles, common dolphins, and African manatees. It is also listed as a natural heritage site threatened by flooding and coastal erosion."}

{"digest":"The Abossey Okai Central Mosque, also called the Accra Central Mosque, is a mosque in the Abossey Okai area of Accra, Ghana. Built in the 1970s, it was set up for the Muslim community in Abossey Okai and nearby areas such as Sabon Zango. After the central mosque at Makola was demolished in the 1980s, this mosque became Accra’s central mosque. It also served for Friday prayers led by the Chief Imam of Ghana."}

{"digest":"Adrar Bous is a massif in the Aïr Mountains on the western edge of the Ténéré Desert in Niger. It is known for archaeological sites studied by J. Desmond Clark, with finds from the Late Acheulean through the Neolithic. Visitors would see sites with microlithic tools, faunal and human remains, and evidence of ritualized feasting by Tenerian cattle pastoralists. Nearby sites include Adrar n'Kiffi, with lake remains, bone and stone tools, and Kiffian pottery, and Agorass n'Tast, with Tenerian artifacts and fauna."}

{"digest":"Darazo is a Local Government Area in Bauchi State, Nigeria, with its administrative center in Darazo town. It covers 3,015 square kilometers and was home to about 251,597 people in the 2006 census. The area is mainly inhabited by the Fulani and Karai-karai. A visitor would not find specific attractions listed in the passage, but the area is described as having traditional local leadership, cultural diversity, and communities where the Zumbun language is spoken. Its history is linked to agriculture and social interaction."}

{"digest":"Plateau State is a state in North Central Nigeria, known for rocks, hills and waterfalls, and for its near-temperate climate. Jos, one of Nigeria’s oldest cities, is a centre for many cultures and has the Jos Wildlife Park, Jos Zoo, the National Museum, the Pottery Hall and the Museum of Traditional Nigerian Architecture. The state also has Assop Falls, Kurra Falls, Wase Rock, the Shere Hills, Riyom Rock, Kahwang Rock Formation and Pandam Game Reserve, noted for wildlife and rivers."}

{"digest":"Kambui Hills Forest Reserve is a 14,335-hectare protected area in Kenema District, about 10 km from Kenema town, with steep slopes rising from 100 to 645 m. It contains forest habitat, plus some savanna and wetland, with mature secondary moist forest and semi-deciduous forest on the slopes. Visitors would mainly see birdlife and wildlife, including over 200 bird species, western chimpanzees, colobus monkeys, sooty mangabeys, Diana monkeys, and African forest elephants. It is also a water catchment area and an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Aïr and Ténéré Natural Reserve is in northern Niger and combines the eastern half of the Aïr Mountains with the western Ténéré desert. A visitor would see a varied landscape of living dunes and remote mountains with little human interaction. It is Africa’s largest protected area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed as in danger. The reserve includes an addax sanctuary and is important for the survival of the critically endangered addax and two other threatened antelopes. It is also an Important Bird Area with 165 recorded bird species."}

{"digest":"Bonthe is a small fishing town at the south end of Sherbro Island and the only substantial settlement there. Visitors can walk around its beautiful but crumbling colonial villas, see the graveyard with the remains of British soldiers who died fighting slave traders, and quickly explore the town. Beyond Bonthe, tracks cross the island, and boat tours go to remote fishing villages, rice paddies, and birdlife. The passage says Bonthe was settled in the 17th century by the Royal African Company and was once a busy port before declining after the 1960s."}

{"digest":"Sandervalia National Museum is Guinea’s national museum in Conakry, in the Sandervalia quarter near Ignace Deen Hospital. Visitors can see a limited display of traditional objects from different regions of Guinea, along with colonial-era objects and statues; one room has masks and musical instruments, and the collection once included masks and a sacred forest. The museum is also used for art exhibitions and other cultural events, with some craft items for sale. It was founded in 1960 to house examples of traditional arts."}

{"digest":"Buracona is a small bay in northwest Sal, Cape Verde, about 5 km north of Palmeira. A visitor would see the bay itself as part of the Buracona-Ragona protected landscape, which covers the coast between Palmeira and Ponta Preta and includes Monte Leste, a 269 m mountain. Its significance in the passage is that it lies within a protected landscape of 5.45 km2."}

{"digest":"Rele Art Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Lagos, Nigeria, with locations on Military Street in Onikan and on Victoria Island. Founded by Adenrele Sonariwo, it is part of the Rele Arts Foundation, a nonprofit organisation. Visitors would see exhibitions by Nigerian-based international artists such as Victor Ehikhamenor, Kelechi Amadi-Obi, and Neec Nonso, as well as shows like The Atlantic Triangle and Tech Meets Art. The gallery is noted for opening a Los Angeles location, the first African gallery there."}

{"digest":"The Cascades de Karfiguéla, also called the Banfora or Karfiguela Falls, are a series of waterfalls on the Komoé River in southwestern Burkina Faso, about 12 km northwest of Banfora. A visitor would see the falls, whose flow is strongest in the rainy season from June to September. The site is one of Burkina Faso’s most important tourism locations, and the Cascades Region takes its name from these waterfalls. The nearby city of Banfora supports tourism linked to the falls."}

{"digest":"Uracane is an island in Guinea-Bissau’s Bissagos archipelago, in the sector of Uno within Bolama Region. It lies northeast of Uno and south of Formosa. The passage gives no visitor activities or sights on the island itself, but identifies it as a populated island with 1,181 people recorded in the 2009 census."}

{"digest":"Rimin Gado is a Local Government Area and town in Kano State, northern Nigeria, about 20 km west of Kano city. It is known for agriculture, rural markets, and developing infrastructure. Visitors can see Rimin Gado Dam, a small dam used as a water source for irrigation and domestic needs, visit traditional open-air markets selling local produce and crafts, walk around nearby villages, and take part in farming during planting or harvest season. The area’s residents are mainly Hausa and Fulani, with farming, livestock rearing, and small-scale trading as main occupations."}

{"digest":"Mopti is a city in Mali and one of the country’s main ports, serving as a gateway to Djenné, Timbuktu, and Dogon Country. A visitor would see a bustling harbour and the market near the mosque in the old part of town. From Mopti, travellers can take a pinasse to nearby Bozo villages or arrange a river trip up to Timbuktu. Tours to Dogon Country can also be organised from there."}

{"digest":"The Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park and Mausoleum is in downtown Accra, Ghana’s capital. It is a five-acre memorial complex dedicated to Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana’s first president, and contains the final remains of Nkrumah and his wife, Fathia. Visitors can see the mausoleum and a museum with objects from different stages of his life. The site marks where Nkrumah declared Ghana’s independence, and its design includes symbolic details such as an upside-down sword, a black star, marble cladding, and surrounding water."}

{"digest":"Judiciary Palace is a palace in Nouakchott, Mauritania, on Avenue Gamal Abdel Nasser. The passage says it stands between the Friday Mosque of Nouakchott and the headquarters of Mauritania Airlines. A visitor would see it as part of this central area, next to the Friday Mosque and the Air Mauritania headquarters. Its significance in the passage is mainly its location and its association with nearby public and religious landmarks."}

{"digest":"Saloum Delta National Park is a 760-square-kilometre national park in Senegal, established in 1976 at the meeting of the Saloum River and the North Atlantic, about 100 km south of Dakar. It lies within a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a Ramsar site, and a biosphere reserve. Visitors would see water, mangroves, saltwater vegetation, savannah and forest, as well as birds such as flamingos, spoonbills, terns and sandpipers. The passage also notes its shellfish farming and local economic importance."}

{"digest":"The Sierra Leone National Museum is the national museum of Sierra Leone, located in central Freetown at the junction of Siaka Stevens Street and Pademba Road. Visitors would see a museum that began before independence, opened in 1957 in the former Cotton Tree Telephone Exchange, and still occupies that original temporary site. It preserves objects of archaeological, ethnographical, historical, and scientific interest. The passage notes its role in national heritage, its 1967 national status, an extension opened in 1987, and the display of the only known photograph of Bai Bureh in 2013."}

{"digest":"The Atewa Range Forest Reserve is a forested hill range in southeastern Ghana near Kibi, running north-south with steep-sided hills and fairly flat summits. It contains about 17,400 hectares of upland evergreen forest, rare in Ghana, and is the source of three major rivers. Visitors would see forest reserve landscapes and, in a broader sense, a site of conservation and eco-tourism efforts. Its significance lies in its ancient soils, globally significant biodiversity, rare birds, primates, butterflies, and critically endangered frog species."}

{"digest":"Rao is a village in northern Senegal, about 15km from Saint-Louis, and the seat of Rao Arrondissement. Visitors would be looking at an archaeological place rather than a sightseeing town. It is known for the burial mound where the “Rao Pectoral” was discovered in 1941. That large golden disc is one of the most impressive artifacts found in Senegal and is linked to the period when the Jolof Empire was founded."}

{"digest":"Ile Oluji is a town in Ondo State, south-west Nigeria. Visitors would see an agrarian town where farmers cultivate cocoa, cassava, yam, maize and oil palm, and where cocoa production and export are major activities. The passage says it is one of the largest cocoa producers and exporters in Nigeria. Its indigenes are Yoruba people, and the town’s monarch is the Jegun of Ile-Oluji, with ancestry linked to the mythical Oduduwa."}

{"digest":"Pandrillus is linked to Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary in Cross River State, formed in May 2000 from part of the former Afi River Forest Reserve. The sanctuary is managed by the Cross River State Forestry Commission with conservation and research support from organisations including Pandrillus. Visitors can hike the mountain, but they should arrange this in advance with the conservation project or local guides, as road conditions and access can change. The terrain is steep and rugged."}

{"digest":"Haute Guinee is a region of Guinea made up of the Faranah and Kankan administrative regions, with about 3 million people in 2014. It borders Mali and is drier than other parts of the country, with a sub-Sahelian character. A visitor would see Kankan, the country’s second city after Conakry and a stop on the road to Bamako. The region also includes the National Park of the Upper Niger, which protects important tracts of forest and savannah, and is home to the Malinke people."}

{"digest":"Janjanbureh is a city in Upriver Gambia. Visitors can see the Senegambian stone circles on the north bank just across from Janjanbureh, near Lamin Koto. The circles are spread across both sides of the Gambia-Senegal border and are thought to have been built around the 8th century to mark grave sites. There are about 1,000 circles, with the main concentration on the Gambian side. They were declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2006."}

{"digest":"The National Cathedral of Ghana is a proposed interdenominational Christian cathedral in Accra, intended as a national place of worship and civic monument for Ghana’s post-independence identity. The site, next to Osu Cemetery, was planned to include a main auditorium, chapels, a baptistery, a Bible museum, an art gallery and a music school. The design by Adjaye Associates draws on Ghanaian architectural motifs, including pitched roofs and timber detailing inspired by Akan and Ashanti craftsmanship, and was planned to seat about 5,000 people. The project has also been the subject of scrutiny over funding and procurement."}

{"digest":"Hope (Esperança) Booker was a Gambian woman linked to the Senegambian coast and the Royal African Company’s trade sphere. Born into child slavery to John Booker, she became his executrix after his death, then married another RAC agent, William Heath, in 1694. She returned to Gambia in 1697, and later was addressed on James Island as Madam Esperance. The passage describes her as a signare, a woman of property, status, and social power, and notes her legacy as a successful woman despite the Atlantic slave trade."}

{"digest":"Cotonou is Benin’s largest city and main port of entry, on the southern coast. It grew from a fishing village under the Dahomey Kingdom into the country’s economic and population centre, and is often treated as the de-facto capital. Visitors can walk the Zongo neighbourhood and its busy main mosque, stroll the beach by day, or visit Fidjirossé’s beachside maquis. Notable sights include Cotonou Cathedral, Place de l’Amazone, Monument Bio Guera, and boat tours to Ganvie, the stilt village on Lake Nokoué."}

{"digest":"The Bura culture, or Bura system, is a set of archaeological sites in the lower Niger River valley of Niger and Burkina Faso, centered in southwest Niger and southeast Burkina Faso. It was an Iron Age civilization dating from the 3rd century AD to the 13th century. Visitors would not see a living settlement but the remains and artifacts found there: clay, iron and stone objects, including ritual terracotta jars, iron arrowheads, beads, brass nose rings, bracelets, and terracotta equestrian statuettes. Its significance lies in its early and distinctive material culture."}

{"digest":"Hann Forest and Zoological Park is a nature reserve in Dakar, in the Hann Bel-Air commune of Senegal. A visitor can see crocodiles, lions, chimpanzees, gazelles, hyenas, reptiles, birds, dromedaries and turtles, along with a botanical garden, an aquarium, an arboretum and an ethnobotanical garden with more than 250 kinds of plants. The passage says it was opened to the public in 1935, helped shelter residents during the Battle of Dakar, and later gained an environmental education center for students."}

{"digest":"The Old Residency Museum is a government-run museum in Calabar, Nigeria, housed in a colonial building first erected in 1884 as the Government House. It was prefabricated in Britain for British officials in the Niger area and later became a museum. Visitors can see a large collection of Nigerian documents and artifacts on the history of the Calabar and Cross River regions and slavery. The building was declared a national monument in 1959 and renovated in 1986."}

{"digest":"Kaouar, or Kawar, is a chain of ten oases in northeast Niger’s southern Sahara, stretching about 75 km along the eastern edge of the Ténéré desert. A visitor would see the oasis towns of Bilma, Dirkou, Aney and Séguédine, and the salt and date production for which the area is known. The passage says Kaouar was once a key caravan route linking the African Sahel with Mediterranean civilisations, and that archaeological sites and rock paintings show habitation dating back about 10,000 years."}

{"digest":"Aran-Orin is a town in Irepodun local government area of Kwara State, North Central Nigeria, near the borders with Osun and Ekiti states. It is about 8 kilometres from Omu-Aran and close to towns including Arandun, Rore, Ipetu, Erinmope and Ilale. The passage says it originated from Ile-Ife and is an Igbomina-speaking Yoruba community. Oil deposits were discovered there in 2011. It is administered with help from the Aran Orin Progressive Union, a group of elected indigenes."}

{"digest":"Ouagadougou Cathedral, the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception of Ouagadougou, is the Roman Catholic cathedral of the archdiocese in Burkina Faso’s capital. Built in the 1930s under apostolic vicar Joanny Thévenoud of the White Fathers and dedicated after two years of construction, it dates from the era of French West Africa. A visitor would see the cathedral itself and, behind it near the car park, an altar to Mary called Ave Maria, with a statue of the Virgin in a carved stone arch."}

{"digest":"The National Museum of Mauritania, also called the National Museum of Nouakchott, is a national museum in Nouakchott. Visitors can see archaeological and ethnographical collections in two galleries, including sherds, arrowheads, local costumes, and objects from different Mauritanian cultures. The museum has two permanent exhibition rooms and a temporary exhibition room. Its archaeological holdings include Mousterian, Aterian and Neolithic artifacts, plus material from excavations in historic cities such as Koumbi Saleh, Aoudaghost, Tichit, Ouadane and Azougui. The two-storey building also houses research and library institutions."}

{"digest":"The Liberation Day Monument is a historic war memorial in Accra, within the Black Star Square complex on 28th February Road. It honours veterans of the Gold Coast Regiment and the Burma campaign of the Second World War. The passage says these veterans later led a peaceful march toward Christiansborg Castle after returning to the Gold Coast, and were shot by British colonial police in 1948, killing seven. The monument marks this event, which helped catalyze Ghana’s path to independence."}

{"digest":"Fort Kongenstein was a Danish trading fort built in 1783 in Ada Foah, Ghana. The passage says most of it has since been washed away by the sea waves, so visitors would mainly see the remains of the fort rather than a complete structure. Ada was once a trade center because its Atlantic Coast and Volta River location allowed goods from the interior to be shipped out efficiently. The fort was built to secure Danish interests against local tribes."}

{"digest":"The Mamelon of Sikasso is a 30-metre-high hill in the heart of Sikasso, Mali, built in the 1880s by King Tiéba Traoré of Kénédougou for royal seating. At the summit is a replica of a fortified multistory structure that once served as a place of work and a traditional court before its destruction during the French conquest. The site was long used for gatherings, court sessions, receiving guests, and observing the surrounding area, and it marked the first flying of the French flag in Sikasso in 1898."}

{"digest":"Fort Gross Fredericksburg is a fortification in Princestown, in Ghana’s Western Region. Built in 1683–1684 by the Brandenburg Africa Company as its headquarters, it is the only fort in Ghana of German construction. A visitor would see a stone fort made with stone imported by sea from Prussia. The passage says it was the site of John Canoe’s resistance against a planned sale to the Dutch, that the Dutch later seized it in 1725 and renamed it Hollandia, and that about 300,000 Africans are believed to have been transported through it."}

{"digest":"Beregadougou Classified Forest is a national park in Burkina Faso covering 50 km2. The passage says it was established in 1953. It also notes that in November 2017, the PADA/REDD+ project, aimed at supporting cashew nut development in the Comoé basin and reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, was launched in Bérégadougou."}

{"digest":"The Praia Cape Verde Temple is a temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Praia, Cape Verde, and the first temple built in the country. Visitors would see a one-story building with a single attached end tower, an understated design inspired by local architecture, and landscaping with gardens, flowering shrubs, shade and palm trees, and walkways. The site also includes a meetinghouse. Its ceremonial spaces include an instruction room, sealing room, and baptistry, and the design uses symbolic elements representing the Praia region."}

{"digest":"Praia de Chaves, also called Praia da Chave, is a about 5 km beach on the western side of Boa Vista in Cape Verde, near Rabil. The northern part has tourist resorts, while the southern part lies in the Morro de Areia Nature Reserve. Visitors can use the beach for surfing, as it is the main spot. The passage also says the island’s arid conditions shaped its history, including late discovery, salt mining, settlement, pirate attacks, and the decline that followed abolition of slavery."}

{"digest":"Anne Pépin was a signare on Gorée in French Senegal, belonging to the Afro-European habitants class. A visitor learning about her would be looking at the island’s colonial and slave-trade history, including the Maison des Esclaves linked to her brother and the large house she lived in. The passage says she held social and economic power through partnerships with European men, inherited wealth from her husband, and was one of the leading figures of the signare community involved in supporting the island’s slave-trade system."}

{"digest":"Kara is a base for visiting Koutammakou, about two hours north, where the village of Nadoba has unique clay-and-straw Tatas. These houses were built to fend off slave traders and now hold farm animals and materials. Visitors can see sacrificial altars, fetishes in the first room, and the Chief Canton’s Tata. The area is described as Togo’s only UNESCO World Heritage Site and its best tourist attraction, though there are no amenities. Kara is also linked to Parc Sarakawa, where guided pickup tours show crocodiles, antelopes, water buffaloes, and a big turtle."}

{"digest":"Bole is a major town in Ghana’s Savannah Region on the main highway linking southern Ghana with the Upper West Region. A visitor would mainly use it as a base for travelling onward to nearby places in Northern Ghana, including Mole National Park to the east, Wa to the north, and Tamale to the northeast. The passage says it is strategically positioned for exploring wildlife, cultural landmarks, and cities in the region."}

{"digest":"Forte de São José is a fort in Porto Inglês, in the south of Maio Island, Cape Verde. Built by the Portuguese around 1743, it was made to protect the town from pirate attacks. Today it is one of the town’s tourist attractions. A lighthouse was added inside the fort in 1887: a white stone tower, 18 metres tall, solar powered, standing 4 metres above sea level, with a 17 km range."}

{"digest":"Wulensi is a small market town and the capital of Nanumba South District in Ghana’s Northern Plains, on the road between Bimbilla and Nkwanta/Kpandai. Visitors would see a busy periodic market, a lorry station, guesthouses, and a town laid out along the main road. About 4–5 km outside town are the seasonal Wulensi Waterfalls in a rocky valley, where swimming may be possible when water is low. The town is also a historic Nanun kingdom settlement and a trading centre for nearby farming communities."}

{"digest":"Dosso is a city in southwestern Niger and the capital of Dosso Region. It is a historic and cultural hub of the Zarma people and was once the seat of the Dosso Kingdom. A visitor can see the Dosso Sultan’s Palace and the Musée Régional de Dosso, and may encounter the annual cure salée festival. The city is also an agricultural center near the Niger River and a crossroads for trade routes connecting Niamey and other regions."}

{"digest":"In Madarounfa Department, Maradi Region, Niger, this site combines a classified forest, a lake, and the Tombs of the 99 Saints. The forest begins 1 km north of the lake and covers 830 hectares, with a landscape of trees and flowers. The 800-hectare lake is home to many bird species. The tombs surround the lake and are used for rituals by local people. The site is listed on UNESCO’s World Heritage Tentative List as a mixed cultural and natural place."}

{"digest":"The Aïr Mountains, or Aïr Massif, are a triangular massif in northern Niger within the Sahara. They rise above the desert as nine almost circular massifs, with flat-topped granite peaks, broad sandy valleys, seasonal wadis, and volcanic features such as the extinct caldera of Arakao, lava flows, cones, tuff rings, and a large ring dike system. The plateau forms an island of Sahel climate supporting pastoral and farming communities, wildlife, and archaeological sites that illustrate the region’s prehistoric past."}

{"digest":"Orlu is a city in southeast Nigeria and the second largest in the region after Owerri. It was the headquarters for the Organisation of African Unity’s humanitarian relief agencies during the Nigeria-Biafra Civil War, and the Nigerian headquarters of the British Cheshire Home is there. A visitor would see a city known for enterprise and industry, the Imo International Market, and institutions such as Imo State University Teaching Hospital and the Nigerian Immigration Training School. Old Orlu is noted for plant and exotic animal resources, monsoon forests, and wildlife reserves."}

{"digest":"Étoile Rouge is a roundabout in Cotonou, mentioned as one of the main places where taxi drivers wait in Benin. Visitors would see taxis gathered here, alongside Dantokpa market and Gare de Jonquet, and can use it to hire a taxi for travel around the city or farther. The passage notes that fixed-route taxis run from Dantokpa through Étoile Rouge toward the Stade de l’Amitié, and east across the lagoon to Akpakpa. It is also a place associated with taxi pickup and negotiation."}

{"digest":"The Sierra Leone River is a river estuary on the Atlantic in western Sierra Leone, formed by the Bankasoka and Rokel rivers. Visitors would see a wide harbour with major ports at Queen Elizabeth II Quay and Pepel, plus islands including Tasso, Tombo and historically important Bunce Island. It separates Freetown from Lungi International Airport, with travel by speed boat or ferry. The estuary is significant as the largest natural harbour in Africa and a Ramsar wetland and Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Lloyd Gwam was a Nigerian historian and Director of the Nigerian National Archives in Ibadan. A visitor would not be seeing a place here, but learning about his life and work: he studied at Government School Asaba, Edo College, Dennis Memorial Grammar School in Onitsha, and University College Ibadan. He worked in the Nigerian Civil Service, served in archival and UNESCO-related roles, and led the Federal Republic of Nigeria’s archives from 1964 until his death in 1965. His publications focused on the National Archives of Nigeria."}

{"digest":"Cova-Paul-Ribeira da Torre Natural Park is a natural park in the east of Santo Antão, Cape Verde, and one of the country’s ten natural parks. It covers the Cova Crater, the upper valleys of Ribeira da Torre and Ribeira do Paul, and Pico da Cruz. A visitor would see a volcanic crater, steep cliffs, escarpments, deep river valleys, forest and farmland. The park has many endemic plants, plus endemic reptiles and birds. Since 2016, it has been on the tentative list of World Heritage Sites."}

{"digest":"The Ouidah Museum of History is a history museum in Ouidah, Benin, housed in the Portuguese Fort of São João Baptista de Ajudá, built in 1721. Visitors can see 11 rooms with around 700 objects and collections on Ouidah’s archaeology, arts and history, including items related to the fort, the Kingdom of Xwéda, the Kingdom of Dahomey, the slave trade and repatriation. The fort was a trading post, later a Catholic mission, and then the Portuguese seat before being annexed in 1961."}

{"digest":"Ada is an area in the Dangme East District of eastern Greater Accra, made up mainly of Ada Foah, Big Ada, and Ada Kasseh. Visitors usually spend time at Ada Foah, by the beach and river estuary. The district has a 45-kilometre coconut-fringed coastline with sandy beaches, though it is affected by erosion and beach litter. The Volta River estuary has islands with marine turtles, birds, crocodiles, monkeys, and mangrove vegetation, and supports water sports. Songor Lagoon is important for salt mining and birdwatching."}

{"digest":"Quartel Jaime Mota is a historical building in Plateau, the historic centre of Praia, Cape Verde, near the Presidential Palace. Built as military barracks between 1823 and 1826, its present Neo-Manueline structure dates from 1872 and was later expanded and altered. After independence it was named for Jaime Mota, a Cape Verdean PAIGC militant killed in Portuguese Guinea. The building was planned for restoration to house a military museum and Ministry of Defence services."}

{"digest":"Yunyoo is a quiet farming town and the capital of Yunyoo-Nasuan District in Ghana’s North East Region. Visitors would see a very rural Guinea savanna landscape with farmland, fallow bush, shea and dawadawa trees, and can walk the main dirt road past the district assembly, market, and lorry station. The market sells yams, maize, livestock, and shea butter, and Konkomba traditional compounds show scattered huts, granaries, and livestock pens. It is significant as a new district capital and a Konkomba area."}

{"digest":"Gumel is a historical town in Jigawa State, Nigeria, known for its cultural heritage and strategic location as a gateway to the northeastern part of the country. Visitors would see an old town with a long history, and the passage notes its past role as a center for trade and commerce. It also remains an important agricultural hub."}

{"digest":"Kaduna is the capital of Kaduna State in north-west Nigeria and a trade centre and major transportation hub for the surrounding agricultural areas, linked by rail and road. Visitors can see Kaduna Polytechnic’s main campus at Tudun Wada, shop at Kaduna Central Market for provisions, furniture, electronics and generators, and visit Barnawa Paradise Park, a private recreational centre with a mini-zoo, gardens, a playground, animals such as monkeys and peacocks, a children’s swimming pool, and spaces for board games and outdoor games. The name comes from the Hausa word for crocodile."}

{"digest":"Agadez is the fifth largest city in Niger and the capital of Agadez Region and the Sultanate of Agadez. It lies in the Sahara desert, and its historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Founded before the 14th century, it grew through trans-Saharan trade and became an important Tuareg city. Visitors would see a desert city where caravans still arrive with salt from Bilma. The passage also notes its long political history, including rule by the Songhai, French colonial occupation, and later Tuareg rebellions."}

{"digest":"Langue de Barbarie is a thin sandy peninsula in western Senegal, beside the Atlantic Ocean and near Saint-Louis. It separates the ocean from the last stretch of the Senegal River. At its southern edge is Langue de Barbarie National Park, a 2,000-hectare area known for many bird species and three kinds of turtle, including the critically endangered hawksbill sea turtle. The passage also says a breach cut in 2003 later widened, turning the southern end into an island and causing loss of land, villages, and tourist resorts."}

{"digest":"Joal-Fadiouth is a city on Senegal’s western coast, on the Petite Côte south of Mbour. Visitors can watch the artisanal fishing port, where boats bring in catches and fresh fish can be bought, and see the house where Léopold Sédar Senghor grew up. Fadiouth, the main attraction, is an island built mainly of sea shells, reached by bridges. Its cemetery is also shell-covered, and Muslims and Christians are buried near each other. The city is linked to Senegal’s first president and to a large artisanal fishing port in West Africa."}

{"digest":"The Henriette-Bathily Women's Museum is a Senegalese museum that was first on Gorée, opposite the House of Slaves museum, and moved in 2015 to Dakar. It was conceived in 1987 and opened in 1994. Housed in a former colonial residence built in 1777, it displays colonial-period objects, farming tools, musical instruments, pottery, basketry, and photographs about women’s daily life. It also highlights Senegalese women’s emancipation and has hosted workshops, literacy courses, and artisanal training for women, including disabled women."}

{"digest":"Kyabobo National Park is a protected mountainous area in Ghana’s Volta Basin near Nkwanta and the Togo border. It lies in a transition zone between forest and savanna, with steep hills, forest, woodland and savanna, plus the Breast Mountains and Mount Kyabobo. Visitors can hike, see waterfalls and the Koue River, and look for wildlife such as buffalo, kob, warthog, baboons and other recorded mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians. The park is also significant for endangered species, including Talbotiella gentii and threatened animals such as elephant and lion."}

{"digest":"Aguadinha is a subdivision of São Filipe on Fogo Island, next to Bila Baxo, and is home to Associação Spartak D'Aguadinha, a sports club founded in 2002. The club’s football team has played in the Premier division and now plays in the Fogo Island League at Estádio 5 de Julho, where it also trains. A visitor would see football, basketball, volleyball and futsal activity connected to the club. Its basketball and volleyball games are played at Polidesportivo Simão Mendes. The club is named after Spartak Moscow but is not affiliated with it."}

{"digest":"Kafountine is a coastal village in Senegal’s Casamance region, where people traditionally live from fishing and rice cultivation. Visitors can see beaches lined with filao trees, stay in camps developed for ecotourism, and take bird-watching or boat trips on the river from the nearby national park. It is also the starting point for canoe excursions to the Karones Islands through dense mangrove channels. Visitors can learn to play djembe or attend a drum concert."}

{"digest":"Cabo da Ribeira is a settlement in the eastern part of Santo Antão, Cape Verde, in the municipality of Paul and within the Cova-Paul-Ribeira da Torre Natural Park. It sits about 500 m above sea level in the upper valley of the Ribeira do Paul, southwest of Pombas. Visitors would see a valley with small-scale agriculture producing sugar cane, coffee, yam, banana, papaya and mango, and the nearby source area of the Ribeira do Paul stream, which runs through a narrow, steep gorge."}

{"digest":"Guembeul Natural Reserve is a 720-hectare faunal reserve about 10 km south of Saint-Louis in the Gandiol region of Senegal. It was designated an IUCN category IV Faunal Reserve in 1983. Visitors would see birds, reptiles, and mammals, and the reserve is a center for reintroduction programs for three species of gazelles. It is also home to the African spurred tortoise. The passage describes it as a natural reserve serving the more conventional European tourist industry."}

{"digest":"The Four Communes of Senegal were Saint-Louis, Dakar, Gorée, and Rufisque, the four oldest colonial towns in French West Africa. A visitor would be looking at places shaped by French colonial rule and the legal status of their African inhabitants, called originaires, with some people later becoming Évolués. The passage notes their political importance: the communes could elect a deputy to the French Parliament, and Blaise Diagne, elected in 1914, helped win citizenship and voting rights for originaires in 1916."}

{"digest":"Gola Rainforest National Park is Sierra Leone’s largest tract of rainforest, covering 71,070 hectares in the east of the country. Visitors would see part of the Upper Guinea Forest and a protected area made up of former forest reserves. The passage says the park is home to more than 330 bird species, over 650 butterfly species, and 49 mammal species, including western chimpanzees, pygmy hippopotamuses, and forest elephants. It is significant as a biodiversity hotspot, an Important Bird Area, and part of the Gola-Tiwai UNESCO World Heritage Site."}

{"digest":"Pinselly Classified Forest is a protected area in Mamou Prefecture in the south-eastern Fouta Djallon Highlands of Guinea, near Ouré-Kaba. Visitors would see dry montane forest, tall-grassed savanna patches, and dense evergreen vegetation with giant trees in moist valleys. The forest shelters forest elephants, hippopotamuses, and many primates and ungulates, including Diana monkey, patas monkey, olive baboon, Western bongo, bushbuck, and red-flanked duiker. It is especially significant as a stronghold for the endangered Western chimpanzee."}

{"digest":"The Richat Structure, or Guelb er Richât, is a large circular geological feature near Ouadane in Mauritania’s Adrar Region, on the Adrar Plateau of the Sahara. Visitors would see a deeply eroded dome about 40 kilometres across, with concentric rings of exposed rock and a central area of breccia. The passage says it contains intrusive and extrusive igneous rocks and exceptional accumulations of Acheulean Paleolithic stone tools. It was selected as one of the IUGS’s 100 geological heritage sites for its scientific value."}

{"digest":"Ribeira da Torre is a torrential stream in northeastern Santo Antão, Cape Verde. It rises in the mountains north of the Cova crater near Rabo Curto and flows north through Xoxo, Fajã Domingas Benta and Lugar de Guene. In Ribeira Grande, it joins the river Ribeira Grande just before it reaches the Atlantic Ocean. Visitors would see the upper valley, which is part of the Cova-Paul-Ribeira da Torre Natural Park, and small-scale खेती of sugar cane, coffee, yam, banana, papaya and mango."}

{"digest":"The Muni-Pomadze Ramsar Site is a wetland in Winneba, Ghana, west of the coastal town and about 55 km west of Accra. Designated a Ramsar site in 1992, it includes the Yenku A and B forest reserves, three seasonal streams, and Muni Lagoon, which surrounds a flood plain and adjacent sand beach. Visitors would see hills, dunes with coconut palms, mangroves, grassland, thickets, and forest. It is also an Important Bird Area and has had degraded mangrove areas restored by local fishing communities."}

{"digest":"Wli Waterfalls is in the Volta Region of Ghana, about 20 km from Hohoe. It is the highest waterfall in Ghana and the tallest in West Africa, with two cascades: an upper fall about 80 metres high and a lower fall about 65 metres. The Agumatsa River forms the falls over sandstone and shale cliffs in the Akwapim-Togo mountain range. Visitors can walk through the Agumatsa wildlife sanctuary and see fruit bats, butterflies, birds, monkeys, and baboons."}

{"digest":"Gadabedji Total Reserve is a nature reserve in central Niger, north of Dakoro in the Maradi Region. Visitors would see Sahelian wooded steppe and grassland south of the Aïr Mountains, along a transhumance route used by cattle, camels, and some wild gazelles. The reserve was created to protect Sahelo-Saharan antelopes, especially scimitar-horned oryx and dama gazelle, which have largely disappeared. It is also recognized as a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 2017."}

{"digest":"Topo de Coroa is a volcanic mountain in the western part of Santo Antão, Cape Verde, and the island’s highest point at 1,979 m. It forms part of a natural park covering 84.92 km2. Visitors would see a volcanic landscape and the source of several streams, including Ribeira de Monte Trigo, which flows west to Monte Trigo. The passage says the area is significant for biodiversity, containing 61% of Cape Verde’s endemic angiosperm plants, with 25% on the red list of endangered species."}

{"digest":"Praça Amílcar Cabral, also called Praça Nova, is an important square in central-northern Mindelo, São Vicente, Cape Verde. Built in 1895 in a then undeveloped part of town, it was renamed after independence in 1975 from Serpa Pinto to Amílcar Cabral, the independence leader of Cape Verde and Guinea-Bissau. A visitor would see the square itself and nearby buildings including the Centro Nacional de Artesanato e Design and the New Building, formerly used by the British telegraph cable company and now housing CV Telecom."}

{"digest":"The Dosso Partial Faunal Reserve is a nature reserve in southwest Niger’s Dosso Region, covering 3,065 square kilometres in the mouth of the Dallol Bosso valley near the W du Niger National Park. Visitors would be in a seasonal wash and ancient riverbed landscape set up to protect wildlife, including African elephants, hippos, gazelles, and the West African giraffe. It is significant as the southern end of the migration path of the last sustainable herd of West African giraffe and provides dry-season forage and habitat."}

{"digest":"Pô is a small town in Burkina Faso’s Volta Delta region, capital of Nahouri province and a border post with Ghana. It is mainly used as a base for excursions in Gurunsi country. From Pô, visitors can go to Kaboré Tambi National Park, the Nazinga game ranch, and villages with traditional architecture such as Tiébélé, Tiakané, Tangassoko, Kaya, and Guelwongo. Nearby Tiébélé has a UNESCO-listed former royal court, while Tangassoko is known for preserved decorative frescoes. Kaboré Tambi once had many elephants but now has few large mammals because of poaching."}

{"digest":"Kamina Funkstation was a large wireless transmitter built near the village of Kamina in German Togoland, now Togo. It was constructed from 1911 to 1914 as part of a German secret communications strategy, designed to link colonial radio stations and reach Germany and other German territories. Visitors to the site would be looking at the remains of a station once powered by its own power plant and huge steel towers. Its significance lies in its wartime role and its destruction on 24/25 August 1914 to stop British and French capture."}

{"digest":"Fazao Malfakassa National Park is the largest of Togo’s three national parks, lying between the Kara and Centrale regions and partly along the border with Ghana. It was created in 1975 from two reserve forests. Visitors go hiking in the rocky hills of the Malfacassa Zone de Chasse, while the Forest Classée Du Fazao holds most of the biodiversity. The park has savanna woodland, gallery forest, submontane forest and grass-covered hilltops, and is notable for birds, antelope and a remnant elephant population."}

{"digest":"Ayum Forest Reserve is a forest reserve in the Asunafo South District of Ghana’s Ahafo Region, established in 1940 and covering 112 square kilometres. It is linked with the Subim and Bonsam Bepo reserves, forming a larger protected area of about 488 square kilometres. Visitors would be in forest habitat that supports a small number of chimpanzees, elephants and other endangered species, as well as snails, nuts and fuelwoods. It is significant for conserving biodiversity in the Guinean Moist Forest Eco-Region."}

{"digest":"Ounjougou is a lieu-dit in the Upper Yamé Valley on the Bandiagara Plateau in Dogon Country, Mali, at the center of an archaeological complex of over a hundred sites. A visitor would see spectacular gullies and natural sections over 10 meters high formed by river erosion, with stratified layers visible in the landscape. The site has yielded rich archaeological and botanical remains, including the earliest pottery found in Africa. It is important for reconstructing settlement patterns and environmental history in West Africa."}

{"digest":"Gbewaa Palace in Yendi is the royal seat of the Yaa Naa, the king of the Kingdom of Dagbon. It stands at Nayilifong along the Yendi-Saboba road and is named after Gbewaa, the patriarch of the Mole-Dagbani people of Ghana. The passage says the palace was burnt and plundered in 1896 during the German invasion of Dagbon, and that redevelopment began when Gariba II cut sod in March 2023."}

{"digest":"Kiffa is the capital of Mauritania’s Assaba region and a busy trading centre on the Route de l’Espoir between Nouakchott and Néma. Visitors would see a large market that draws goods, traders, herders and travellers from Mauritania and nearby countries, and the city’s colourful Kiffa beads, traditionally handmade from powdered glass. It also serves as the main base for exploring Assaba’s mountains, dunes, oasis valleys, lakes, springs and seasonal grasslands where the Sahara meets the Sahel."}

{"digest":"Umuleri is an ancient Igbo town in Anambra State, South East Nigeria, in Anambra East Local Government Area and the Omambala valley. It is part of the Greater Onitsha Metropolis and is known for its Eri clan lineage and connection to the legendary founder Eri. A visitor would find football fields, worship centres for prayer services, crusades and night vigils, and a hospital or health centre. The town also has festivals such as the Yam Festival and Masquerade parade, and is bordered by the Anambra River and nearby villages including Anam, Nteje, Nando and Nsugbe."}

{"digest":"Bassari Country in southeast Senegal is a well-preserved multicultural landscape formed by the interaction of human activity and the natural environment. It includes three areas: Bassari–Salémata, Bedik–Bandafassi, and Fula–Dindéfello, each with its own physical characteristics. A visitor would see this grouped cultural landscape rather than a single site. Its significance is that the Bassari Country and its Bassari, Fula and Bedik Cultural Landscapes were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2012."}

{"digest":"Fort Augustaborg was a Danish fort on the eastern Gold Coast in what is now Ghana, about 15 km east of Fort Christiansborg near present-day Teshie. Built in 1787 and named for Princess Louise Augusta of Denmark, it was constructed to resist Portuguese attacks and later served as a post in the Atlantic slave trade. It was one of five Danish forts purchased by Queen Victoria in 1850 and is now part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site with other Ghanaian forts and castles."}

{"digest":"Aburi is a town of about 19,000 people on the Akwapim Hills in Ghana’s Eastern region, and it is home to the Aburi Botanical Gardens. Visitors would see a town at higher altitude with a cooler climate than nearby Accra. Aburi is also among the places that celebrate the Odwira festival, which marks a historic victory over the Ashanti in 1826 and is described as a time of spiritual purification, renewal, and protection."}

{"digest":"Samori Ture was a Malinke Muslim cleric, military strategist, and founder of an empire that extended across present-day Guinea and parts of Sierra Leone, Mali, Côte d’Ivoire, and Burkina Faso. He is known for organizing his empire around Islamic principles and resisting French colonial rule in West Africa from 1882 until his capture in 1898. The passage also notes his early life in Sanankoro, his military training, and his rise as a warrior, and that he was the great-grandfather of Guinea’s first president, Ahmed Sékou Touré."}

{"digest":"Ilhéu dos Pássaros is a small uninhabited islet in the Cape Verde archipelago, about 700 m off the northeastern coast of Boa Vista near Praia das Gatas. It is low and flat, covered with sedimentary material and sand, and linked to the main island by reefs and volcanic rocks. The islet and surrounding marine area form a protected reserve. Its main significance is as an important nesting site for white-faced storm petrels and band-rumped storm petrels."}

{"digest":"Ibokun, also known as Ilemure, Ilu Obokun, or Ilu'bokun, is a town in Osun State in southwest Nigeria and the headquarters of Obokun. The passage says it was named for a warrior who defended the town against attacks from neighbouring fighters. It also links the name Obokun to a Yoruba story about Obokun, the youngest son of Oduduwa, who travelled from Ifẹ to get sea water to treat his father’s blindness."}

{"digest":"Nok is a village in Kaduna State, Nigeria, and the place after which the Nok culture was named. It is where Nok terracotta were discovered in large concentrations, and similar figurines found across central Nigeria took the village’s name. Visitors can see a museum with figurines, images, the furnaces used in making them over 2,000 years ago, and the house of Bernard Fagg. The area also has mountain scenery, caves used as wartime hiding places, and the Tree of Life story."}

{"digest":"Cidade Velha is a city on the south coast of Santiago, Cape Verde, and the oldest settlement in the country, founded in 1462 by Portuguese traders. It was the former capital, once called Ribeira Grande, and is now the seat of the Ribeira Grande de Santiago municipality. Visitors can see parts of the original plan, including a royal fortress, two churches, and a 16th-century town square. It was a major port in colonial trade and the slave trade, and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site."}

{"digest":"Draw River Forest Reserve is a forest reserve in Ghana, established in 1937 and covering 235 km2. The Draw River runs through its eastern part, and the reserve lies at an elevation of 75 m above sea level. A visitor would see a forest reserve with a river passing through it. Its significance is that BirdLife International has designated it an Important Bird Area because it supports significant populations of many bird species."}

{"digest":"Fort Elize Carthago was a Dutch West India Company fort built in 1702 on a hill at the mouth of the Ankobra River, near Fort Saint Anthony on the Western Gold Coast. Today, only ruins remain, reachable by a pathway from the Ankobra Beach Hotel. Visitors go to see the ruins and panoramic views. The site was linked to the gold trade through the Ankobra River, and the fort was later abandoned in 1711 and destroyed in 1712. Archaeological excavations were carried out in 1999 and 2011."}

{"digest":"Dondoli Mosque is a mosque in the village of Dondoli in Wa, in Ghana’s Upper West Region. Built in the 19th century in Sudano-Sahelian style, it is now in partial ruins. The passage says it was founded by Karimafa, a migrant from Mali, and was once called Karimafa Mosque. It reflects the spread of Islam in northern Ghana along gold trade routes, where mosques also served as resting points for Islamic traders."}

{"digest":"Dalla Hill, also spelled Dala, is a 534-metre hill in Kano, Kano State, Nigeria, with a stairway of 101 steps from bottom to top. Visitors would see the hill itself and the route up it. The passage says it was the site of a seventh-century iron-working community and later the Tsumburbura shrine. It is important in Kano’s history: Kano was originally known as Dala, and the hill is tied to Barbushe, Hausa folklore, and the Bayajidda legend."}

{"digest":"Dhar Tichitt is a line of sandstone cliffs in southwestern Mauritania’s Sahara, known for a series of Neolithic archaeological sites. It is one of the oldest known occupation sites in West Africa and includes about 500 settlements linked to the Tichitt culture. Visitors would see steep cliffs, sandy flats, and interdunal depressions, but the passage mainly describes the remains: drystone house-and-granary compounds, livestock enclosures, and circumvallation walls. The sites show pastoralist and farming life, and may have been a regional center for a hierarchical social structure."}

{"digest":"Akaa Falls is a waterfall in Ghana near Akyeremanteng village in the Akuapem North District, about 21 kilometres northeast of Koforidua in the Eastern Region. It is a 60-metre cascade surrounded by dense vegetation. The falls are about seven kilometres from Boti Falls and take their source from the Boti River, the same river that feeds Boti Falls. The passage also notes that Akaa Falls and Boti Falls are waterfalls in the area."}

{"digest":"The Asubima Forest Reserve is a 7,870-hectare protected forest near Akumadan in Ghana’s Ashanti region, established in 1945. It lies 9 kilometers east of Akumadan and sits at the northern edge of the semi-deciduous forest zone. Visitors would see a reserve focused on preserving Ghanaian tree species and on reforesting degraded land. The passage says programs there include nurseries, model plantations, and interventions against logging, wildfires, and illegal farming, with local farmers working as plantation workers, guards, or fire brigade members."}

{"digest":"Ashanti-Kwahu is a region in Ghana covering much of southwest Ghana, bordering Côte d’Ivoire, and includes the ancient kingdom of Ashanti and the Kwahu Plateau. Visitors can see kente weaving towns in Adanwomase, wood carvings and arts and crafts in Ahwiaa, the Ashanti royal family in Kumasi, mining in Obuasi, beadmaking in Somanya, and Bui National Park for hippopotamuses, river scenery, mountains, islands, and birdlife."}

{"digest":"The Abidjan Ivory Coast Temple is a Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints temple in Abidjan, in Cocody City. It was the first temple in Ivory Coast and the seventh in Africa. Visitors could attend the public open house held before its dedication, and the passage describes its one-story form, attached spire with a statue of the angel Moroni, and Mid-Century Modern design. It was designed by FFKR Architects, with exterior details reflecting both the Abidjan region and African tribal decorations."}

{"digest":"Providence Baptist Church is a historic Baptist church in Monrovia, Liberia. Founded in 1821 by early settlers, it is the oldest church in Liberia and the second-oldest Baptist church in Africa. Visitors would see the 1839 building still in use and the larger modernist church completed in 1976 beside it. The church was the site where Liberia’s Declaration of Independence and Constitution were adopted in 1847, and it is recognized as a national shrine for its role in independence."}

{"digest":"Hi Impact Planet, also called Hi Impact Amusement Park, is an amusement, theme park and resort on the outskirts of Lagos in Ogun State along the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway. Visitors can use indoor and outdoor, wet and dry attractions including bumper cars, bumper boats, rides such as the Haunted House, Vertical Swing, Spring ride, Alien-themed and Transformers rides, an ice rink, animatronics with semi-live lions and gorillas, a souvenir court, and an IMAX cinema. The park also has a clinic, banking services, a hotel, food courts, and a large multipurpose hall."}

{"digest":"The Okomfo Anokye Sword Site in Kumasi is built around a sword said to have been placed in the middle of the Ashanti empire by Okomfo Anokye, a legendary Ashanti fetish priest. Visitors can go to the hospital grounds where the site was created in 1996 around the sword. The passage says many people have tried and failed to remove it, and that the site is associated with Komfo Anokye Hospital, named after Anokye."}

{"digest":"Agrour Amogjar is a 690 m peak near the Amogjar Pass on the Adrar plateau in central Mauritania. Visitors would see small natural shelters containing damaged rock paintings, some protected by an enclosure. The panels include geometric circles with sunburst designs, handprints, wildlife such as giraffe, lion and crocodile, cattle herds, human group scenes, and a frieze of dancers. The paintings are noted as heterogeneous, with eight recorded stylistic groups ranging from the pastoral period to more recent graffiti."}

{"digest":"Popenguine is a village in Senegal’s Cap Vert-Thies region, on the Atlantic coast about 70 km south of Dakar on the Petit Cote. Visitors can see its natural reserve and sandy beach, and the reserve is the main tourist draw. The reserve, created in 1986 through the efforts of a local women’s group, protects 1,500 hectares of plants, birds, and other animals. Popenguine is also significant for the sighting of the Black Madonna and an annual pilgrimage that brings Christians from Senegal and nearby countries."}

{"digest":"Gabú is a city in Guinea-Bissau. It is described as a small colonial centre with a Catholic church. From Gabú, travellers can use a dirt road to the Pirada border with Senegal, and it is also possible to go on to Guinea-Conakry. Taxis to Labé in Guinea cost 15,000 CFA plus 3,000 CFA for one piece of luggage, and the journey can take up to 16 hours on bumpy, dusty mountain roads."}

{"digest":"Keta is a coastal town and the capital of Keta Municipal District in Ghana’s Volta Region. Visitors would see a town with a fishing-village origin and a later history as a trading post, with Fort Prizenstein built by the Danes after the 1784 Anlo-Danish War. The passage also notes missionary activity nearby in 1853, Hausa Constabulary based there from 1874, and a later community of Hausa traders. Keta is identified as one of the old Ewe settlements, founded by descendants of Torgbui Wenya."}

{"digest":"Lake Nokoué is a lake in southern Benin, partly fed by the Ouémé and Sô rivers. Cotonou lies on its southern border, and Ganvié is on the northern edge. Visitors would see a broad, shallow lake used for artisanal fishing in dugout canoes and for Acadja fish-breeding facilities. Fishing supports local economic activity and is best when water levels are low between November and June. The lake is also important for wildlife, with at least 78 fish species, birds, and otters."}

{"digest":"Dori is a town in north Burkina Faso, with about 18,000 people. It is known for its herders and its popular livestock markets. A visitor would see a place shaped by water and sand: large barrages nearby, smaller ones forming in the rainy season, and sand that makes travel difficult, especially by bike in the dry season. The town is linguistically and ethnically mixed, with Fulfulde and Mooré widely spoken, along with French and other languages in different neighborhoods."}

{"digest":"MKO Abiola Stadium is a multi-use stadium in Abeokuta, Nigeria, used mostly for football matches. Visitors would see matches played there, as it is the home ground of Gateway F.C. and Abeokuta Stormers SC. The stadium holds 10,000 people. Its name refers to Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola, a businessman, publisher, politician and aristocrat from Abeokuta, Ogun State."}

{"digest":"Tsenku Falls is a waterfall near Dodowa in Ghana’s Greater Accra Region, about 39 km from Accra. It drops about 250 feet over stratified rocks into a cool, clean pool with a large tilapia population. The falls, also called Wuruduwurudu, lie in the Po stream valley and join the Sanyade and Popotsi streams before the water meanders into the sea. The waterfall is located in Dodowa Forest, a historical forest where the Katamanso War ended."}

{"digest":"The Portuguese Chapel of Albreda is a Catholic chapel built by Portuguese explorers in the fifteenth century in Albreda, now in The Gambia. It stands in ruins about 100 metres west of the settlement, with more than half of its walls still present and the back wall intact, topped by a metal cross. Stabilized for protection in 2000, it is one of the oldest buildings in West Africa and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site."}

{"digest":"Old Oyo National Park in Nigeria covers 2,512 km², mostly in Oyo State with some in Kwara State. It is named after Oyo-ile, the ancient political capital of the Oyo Empire, and contains the ruins of that city. Visitors can see lowland plains, granite outcrops, isolated hills, caves, rock shelters, and rivers including Ogun, Owu, Owe, and Tessi. The passage says it is unique among Nigeria’s national parks for its archaeological, cultural, and historical significance, and notes that West African wild dogs no longer live there."}

{"digest":"Monkey Island is a mangrove island in Liberia where lab chimpanzees were abandoned in 2005 and later colonised the island. A visitor would see the chimpanzees; the passage says to do nothing else. The island’s significance comes from its history: a research lab began hepatitis work on chimpanzees in 1974, the lab closed in 2005, and the chimps have since been cared for by local caretakers and Humane Society International. As of 2019, there were 66 chimpanzees there."}

{"digest":"The Tomb of Askia in Gao, Mali, is believed to be the burial place of Askia Muhammad I, a Songhai emperor, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built at the end of the fifteenth century, the complex includes a pyramidal tomb, two mosques, a cemetery and an assembly ground. Visitors would see a 17-metre mud monument in Sudano-Sahelian style, still used as a place of worship and a public cultural centre. It is the largest pre-colonial architectural monument in Gao."}

{"digest":"Eruwa is a town and the headquarters of Ibarapa East Local Government Area in Oyo State, south west Nigeria. It is also the headquarters of Ibarapa, a group of seven towns.
