The town is characterised by many hills and has a monarchy headed by the Eleruwa, assisted by chiefs and ward heads called Baale. Visitors would see Adeseun Ogundoyin Polytechnic, schools, administrative rest houses, and a native court. The passage notes Eruwa’s historic importance as a leading town in Ibarapa district."}

{"digest":"Gunjur is a small rural town on the Atlantic Ocean in The Gambia, far from the northern resort areas. Daily life is described as traditional and largely unchanged for decades. A visitor can go to Gunjur Madina to see a lively fishing village with brightly painted pirogues and a fisheries plant, or explore Gunjur beach, reached by a sandy road at the bus stop. The passage also notes that electricity arrived in 2013."}

{"digest":"Lake Dem is a small lake in northern Burkina Faso, north of Kaya, south of the Sahel Reserve, and south-east of Lake Bam. It is about 5 km long and 2 km wide, at an elevation of 304 m. The passage does not describe visitor activities, but notes that the lake drains into the White Volta and has been designated a Ramsar site since 2009, showing its protected wetland significance."}

{"digest":"Bakel is a remote border town in northern Tambacounda Region, Senegal, on the Senegal River opposite Gouraye, Mauritania. Founded in the 18th century by Ndiaye family migrants, it later became closely tied to Soninke culture. Visitors would see the Fort de Faidherbe, built in 1820, with rusting cannons overlooking the river, lively marketplaces, painted pirogues carrying goods to and from Mauritania, and colonial buildings by the water. The town is an active river port and cultural crossroads."}

{"digest":"Nadowli is a town in Ghana’s Upper West Region and the capital of Nadowli-Kaleo District. The district is centred on subsistence mixed farming, local community markets, and rural administrative governance. A visitor would be in the Ghanaian Northern Plains near borders with Jirapa Municipal, Wa West and Wa Municipal, Daffiama-Bussie-Issa, and Côte d’Ivoire. The passage also lists nearby places associated with visits from Nadowli, including Wa Naa Palace, Wechiau Community Hippo Sanctuary, Mole National Park and Larabanga, Mushroom Rocks in Wulling, Nandom Cathedral, and Gwollu Slave Defense Wall."}

{"digest":"De Ruyter Stone is a national monument in Freetown, Sierra Leone. It is a rock underground on the coast that was carved into by Michiel de Ruyter in 1664 during the Second Anglo-Dutch War, after his force arrived to destroy British settlements. Visitors would see the stone itself and its original inscription, along with hundreds of later writings and drawings made by slaves who drank from the water above it, including paddles, boats, stone pillars, and other objects. It was proclaimed a historical monument in 1948."}

{"digest":"Central Senegal is a region in Senegal with several towns and delta islands. In Foundiougne, visitors can take canoe trips through mangroves, see birds and islands of the Saloum, and find fishing, especially shrimp fishing north of town. Kaolack has a huge covered market and a gris-gris market, and it is the country’s transport hub. Mar Lodj is a quiet rural island where rural life and traditional wrestling can be experienced. Palmarin is near the Delta du Saloum National Park, where mangrove channels can be explored by kayak. Touba is known for the Grand Magal and the Great Mosque."}

{"digest":"Tiagba is a village in southern Ivory Coast on the north shore of Ébrié Lagoon, in the Jacqueville area. It is known for its traditional houses built on stilts. Visitors can take pirogue canoe rides and spend nights in the old lakeside houses on stilts. The passage also notes that Tiagba was once a commune, but this status was abolished in March 2012."}

{"digest":"Akwamufie Palace, also known as Bogyawe Palace, is the official residence and seat of the Akwamuhene of the Akwamu people in Akwamufie, Eastern Region, Ghana, along the Volta River. Visitors can see its museum and traditional monument, which serve as a tourist attraction. The palace holds artifacts including the key to Christiansborg Castle taken in 1693, and the bulletproof lion-skin war cloth called “Mahony.” It is significant as the center from which Odeneho Kwafo Akoto III has led the Akwamu kingdom since 2011."}

{"digest":"Formosa is an island in the Bissagos Islands of Guinea-Bissau, within the sector of Caravela. It covers 140 km2, measures 19.9 km long and up to 10 km wide, and forms almost one island with Ponta and Maio, separated by creeks. A visitor would see an island with settlements rather than a described attraction; the largest village is Abú. The passage gives its significance as a populated island in the Bissagos group, with 1,873 inhabitants recorded in the 2009 census."}

{"digest":"Tano Nimri Forest Reserve is a protected forest area in south-western Ghana, established in 1935 and covering 206 km2. It lies between the Nimri and Tano rivers, with rugged ground, steep slopes, and valleys that flood in rainy periods. The southern third has wet evergreen forest, while the rest is moist evergreen forest. Visitors would mainly encounter forest terrain and birdlife; the reserve is designated an Important Bird Area because it supports significant populations of many bird species, and western chimpanzees are thought to be present."}

{"digest":"Lohen Forest Park is a forest park in The Gambia, established on January 1, 1954. It covers 85 hectares and lies at about 40 metres above sea level. The passage gives its geographic position as 13°32'30\"N, 16°21'51\"W. No visitor activities, facilities, or wildlife details are provided in the passage, so its significance is limited to being a named forest park with a defined size and location."}

{"digest":"Boki is a local government area in Cross River State, southeastern Nigeria, bordering Cameroon and neighbouring Ogoja, Obudu, Obanliku, Ikom and Etung. It is described as peaceful and rural, with 6 traditional clans and 11 political wards. Visitors can see or visit Afi Mountain, Drill Ranch, the Buanchor canopy walkway, Kende Esua Lake, Njua Banor stone and rock, an irrigation dam, and Bishop’s Sam cabin. The area is noted for tropical rainforest, drill monkeys, fertile soil, and cash crops. It also holds an annual new yam festival."}

{"digest":"Sokone is a town in the Fatick region of central Senegal, in the southeastern Sine-Saloum Delta amid mangroves. A visitor can stop there between Kaolack and Banjul, see old colonial peanut warehouses, fields of peanuts and other crops, and take part in the Wednesday weekly market. People also swim in the salty delta river, relax in the shade, and learn to make Senegalese tea with hosts. Nearby are Baumbougar’s ancient baobab tree and Ndiafe Ndiafe, the original village from which Sokone and surrounding villages descend."}

{"digest":"Bandiagara is a city in Dogon Country, Mali, and the main entry point for treks into the area. Visitors can stock up on supplies, sleep, and find guides or drivers there, though these items are said to be more expensive because of the town’s proximity to the treks. The town itself has few sights, but the main administration building at the center roundabout is noted. The nearby Cliff of Bandiagara was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989."}

{"digest":"Marahoué National Park is a national park in central Ivory Coast, west of Bouaflé, covering 1,010 km2. It was established in 1968 and lies partly along the Marahoué River on terrain of low hills and valleys. The passage says visitors would find gallery forests, forest remnant patches, savannas with scattered trees, and wetlands around pools and watercourses. It also notes the park has lost nearly all its forest cover through logging, settling, and agricultural conversion, leaving it no longer suitable habitat for chimpanzees and many other large animals."}

{"digest":"Linonghin is a village in the Kogho Department of Ganzourgou Province in central Burkina Faso. A visitor would see a rural settlement, though the passage gives no attractions or activities there. Its main significance is historical: on August 11, 1974, it was the site of Burkina Faso's deadliest airliner crash, when an Air Mali Ilyushin Il-18V made a forced landing after running out of fuel, killing 47 of the 60 people on board."}

{"digest":"Musée de Manega is a museum in the village of Manega, about 55 km northwest of Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Founded and curated by Frédéric Pacéré Titinga, it specializes in the arts and musical instruments of Burkina Faso. Visitors would see the Boura flutes, around 40 funeral pieces, terracotta jars, bracelets, ritual objects from the Niger Valley dating from the 2nd to the 11th century, and 200-year-old Mossi rifles."}

{"digest":"Ouahigouya is a large town in north Burkina Faso, near the Mali border, and the fourth largest city in the country. It is the final major Burkinabe city on the route to Mali, so there is a steady flow of tourists and commercial travelers. Founded in 1757, it is the capital of Yatenga region and a center of Mossi culture, where Mooré is commonly spoken. Visitors can see Naaba Kango’s tomb, go to the cinema, watch occasional football matches, or swim at Hotel de L’Amitie. A large barrage lies north of town."}

{"digest":"The Fish Statue, officially called The Fish, Epe, is a sculpture of two giant fish at Lekki-Epe T-Junction in Epe, Lagos. It is mounted on a rectangular plinth marked “EPE.” Visitors would see the monument as a roadside landmark. The passage says it represents Epe’s fishing culture and its role as an export point for fish in Lagos, with fishing described as the main occupation of indigenes and the area as a center for fishing, marine transportation, and jobs."}

{"digest":"Ribeira do Paul is a seasonal stream in the northeastern part of Santo Antão, Cape Verde. It rises northeast of the Cova crater near Cabo da Ribeira, then runs through a narrow, steep gorge past the settlements of Campo de Cão and Eito before reaching the Atlantic at Pombas. The upper valley is part of Cova-Paul-Ribeira da Torre Natural Park. Visitors would see the valley’s small-scale agriculture, including sugar cane, coffee, yam, banana, papaya and mango."}

{"digest":"Togba was a town in Mauritania’s Hodh El Gharbi region, now known from its ruins. Visitors today would see the remains recorded by French archaeologist Raymond Mauny in 1949. Mauritanian oral history says it was founded by Tajakant refugees after Tinigui was destroyed in internal tribal conflict, probably in the 15th or 16th century. The town may have survived until about 1905 before being abandoned. French archaeologists described the ruins as “very recent.”"}

{"digest":"Essouk is a small village and commune in Mali’s Kidal Region, northwest of Kidal in the Adrar des Ifoghas massif. Nearby, 2 km northeast of the village, are the ruins of medieval Tadmekka, which stretch over a kilometre in the Essouk valley. A visitor would see desert ruins rather than a large settlement; the commune is sparsely populated and mostly home to nomadic pastoralists. Tadmekka was an important trans-Saharan trade entrepôt from the 9th to 15th centuries, and a stopping place for caravans before entering the Sudan."}

{"digest":"Lagoa do Rabil is a wetland site on Boa Vista in Cape Verde, at the mouth of the seasonally flowing Ribeira do Rabil near the town of Rabil. A visitor would see the river mouth, the lagoon, surrounding dunes, and vegetation dominated by Tamarix, Cyperus, Zygophyllum and Euphorbia species. The site supports Iago sparrows, several waders including Eurasian spoonbill, and endemic lizards Hemidactylus bouvieri and Chioninia stangeri. It has been recognised as a wetland of international importance under the Ramsar Convention since 2005."}

{"digest":"Emure-Ekiti is a town in Ekiti State, South West Nigeria. The passage says visitors would see a town made up of four ancient quarters and a monarch, the Elemure, who is one of the Sixteen crowned Obas in Ekiti. Its history is traced to Ile-Ife, and its name comes from a story about gifting a fern plant called Imu. The town had an estimated population of 94,264 in the 2006 census."}

{"digest":"UTA Flight 772 refers to the crash site of a scheduled international passenger flight that broke up over the Sahara and fell into the Ténéré desert near Bilma, Niger. A visitor would see the desert area where debris was scattered over hundreds of square miles after a suitcase bomb exploded in the cargo hold. All 170 people on board were killed. It is significant as the deadliest aviation incident in Niger."}

{"digest":"Taï National Park is a national park in Ivory Coast and one of the last areas of primary rainforest in West Africa. It was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site because of its diverse flora and fauna. Visitors would see tropical evergreen forest, swamp forest in the northwest, rivers that widen in the wet season and shrink in the dry season, and granite inselbergs such as Mount Niénokoué. The park is significant for threatened species including pygmy hippopotamus, olive colobus monkeys, leopards, chimpanzees, and Jentink's duiker."}

{"digest":"Bo is Sierra Leone’s second city and the main city of the Southern region. It is known for having remained untouched during the war, because a citizen militia kept rebel soldiers out for the full 10 years. Visitors will find little to see in the city itself, and many use it as a stopover. The area has small-scale diamond mining, which may be worth visiting."}

{"digest":"Arli National Park, often called Arly, is a national park in Tapoa Province, southeastern Burkina Faso, adjoining Pendjari National Park in Benin and the Singou Reserve. Visitors can see gallery forests, savanna woodland, sandstone hills, pools and waterholes, including Tounga, where hippos often gather. The park is home to elephants, hippos, lions, buffaloes, monkeys, warthogs and antelopes. It is part of an important bird area and has been designated a Ramsar site for its wetlands."}

{"digest":"Northern Niger covers Niger’s Saharan territory. Its main places include Agadez, the largest city in Saharan Niger, Arlit, and Bilma, Chirfa, and Iferouane, each serving as a gateway to desert regions or reserves. The Aïr and Ténéré National Nature Reserve is noted for desert landscapes, though it is not safe for travel. Termit & Tin Toumma National Nature and Cultural Reserve protects wildlife and nomadic culture. The Cure Salee at In-gall is a yearly gathering of Tuareg and Wodaabe peoples, with market, social, and courtship rituals."}

{"digest":"Somanya is the capital of Yilo Krobo Municipal District in Ghana’s Eastern Region, about 50 km north of Accra’s edge. It is the largest city in a rural farming area, surrounded by smaller suburbs and villages. Visitors would see a warm, humid town where farming dominates the surrounding land, and where Dangme is commonly spoken. The passage also notes nearby places and events: the Kloyosikplemi festival on Krobo Mountain south of the city, the University of Environment and Sustainable Development in New Somanya, and Boti Falls at Boti-Okwenya."}

{"digest":"Buba is a city in Guinea-Bissau with about 8,600 people. A visitor would find a place where fishing, agriculture and trade support the local economy, with rice, peanuts and maize grown and shifting agriculture practiced nearby. The passage notes construction of a deepwater port intended to export bauxite. Buba was once considered as a possible capital city under Kumba Yala, but the plan was dropped after a coup. It is also near Lagoas de Cufada Natural Park, one of the country’s largest protected areas."}

{"digest":"Dia Shoma in Mali is an archaeological site associated with early settlement and pottery evidence. Visitors would not find a modern tourist attraction described here, but the passage says the area has pottery assemblages, different vessel types, and burials dating to about 800 to 1000 AD. Studies of ceramics and funerary practices suggest cultural diversity, mixed economy, and settlement by several incoming population groups, probably from the northwest and from Dhar Tichitt-Walata. It is significant for evidence about early inhabitants, rice cultivation, pastoralism, aquatic resources, and differences from Djenné-Djenno."}

{"digest":"Ségou is a city in the Segou region of Mali, often considered the country’s second city and one of its most important ports. Visitors can walk from the government district to the waterfront and port, where colonial buildings are said to be the most impressive architecture in Mali. The Craft centre on the Mopti road offers guided explanations of how bogolan clothes are made and a chance to try making them. The passage also notes the annual Festival sur le Niger, with music and dance."}

{"digest":"Artists Alliance Gallery, also called Omanye House, is an art centre in Labadi in Ghana’s Greater Accra Region, established by Ablade Glover. Visitors can browse an artist-run gallery spread over three floors, with sculptures, fabrics and paintings. The works range from inexpensive wooden artefacts to expensive paintings by leading Ghanaian artists, and the passage notes that browsing is relaxed and without pressure to buy. It is also a place where Glover’s works are held, and it has shown exhibitions such as a 2014 portfolio of 84 works."}

{"digest":"Pedra de Lume is a village on the east coast of Sal, Cape Verde, about 5 km east of Espargos. Visitors would see a small port, a lighthouse, and the salt evaporation ponds in the crater of an extinct volcano. The passage says the waters in the lake rise from deep in the earth. The salinas have been exploited since the 18th century, with salt production once flourishing, later declining, then revived on a small scale for beauty products and thalassotherapy. The salinas and crater form a protected landscape."}

{"digest":"Tichit is a village in central southern Mauritania at the foot of the Tagant Plateau, known for vernacular architecture, date farming, and a small museum. Visitors would see the village itself and its barren surroundings near an airport, with a long sandstone cliff formation nearby. The area is significant for the Dhar Tichitt archaeological sites, including the oldest surviving archaeological settlements in West Africa and the oldest stone-built settlements south of the Sahara, with stone buildings and rock art linked to early agropastoral communities."}

{"digest":"Falgore Game Reserve is a protected ecosystem in southern Kano State, about 150 kilometers from Kano city, spanning Tudun Wada, Doguwa and Sumaila and reaching the boundaries with Kaduna and Bauchi states. It covers about 1,000 square kilometers and is crossed by the River Kano in the northern guinea savanna belt. Visitors can see rocks, the rapids of River Kano, and the ghost town of Falgore with traditional architecture. The reserve conserves savanna species and helps regulate silting that threatens Tiga Dam."}

{"digest":"Monte Caçador and Pico Forcado Protected Countryside is a protected area in the eastern part of Boa Vista, Cape Verde, covering 3,357 hectares. It contains a small mountain range made up of Monte Caçador, Pico Forcado and the lower Mesa Cágado. The passage says it is the most important mountain formation on the island, though not the highest. Visitors would be looking at a rock formation of phonolitic deposits over the basaltic Fundo de Figueiras Formation."}

{"digest":"Paul is a municipality in northeastern Santo Antão, Cape Verde, with its seat in Pombas. A visitor would see a rugged landscape of mountain valleys cut by the rivers Ribeira do Paul, Ribeira das Pombas, Ribeira de Gil, Ribeira da Janela, Ribeira do Penedo and Ribeira da Aguada. The municipality includes part of the Cova-Paul-Ribeira da Torre Natural Park, and its highest point is Pico da Cruz at 1,585 m. The passage also notes Paul’s shifting municipal borders and its association with Antoninho Travadinha and Josefina Chantre."}

{"digest":"Southern Benin is the lowland coastal region of Benin near the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Guinea. It includes Cotonou, the country’s largest city and economic hub, and Porto-Novo, the official capital. Visitors can see Ganvie, a lake village on stilts, Grand-Popo, a quiet fishing and beach town with boat trips on the Mono River and birdlife, and Lokossa, known for fishing communities and boat trips on a large coastal lake. Ouidah has the historic Route des Esclaves linked to the Atlantic slave trade."}

{"digest":"The German Cemetery of Mango is a historic cemetery in Mango, in Togo’s Savanes Region. Visitors would see the graves of three German soldiers—Wilhelm Bierwerth, Henrich Werner and Theodor Heitman—who were stationed at Sansaanné, now Mango, and died in the late 19th century. The cemetery is linked to German colonial presence in northern Togo and is listed among Togo’s protected historic and cultural sites. It was renovated in 1990."}

{"digest":"Fort Saint Anthony, or Fort Santo Antonio, is a fort near Axim in Ghana built by the Portuguese in 1515. The Dutch captured it in 1642, enlarged it, and kept it as part of the Dutch Gold Coast until handing it to the British in 1872. A visitor can see the fort, now public property. Its history reflects European trade and exploitation on the Gold Coast; it was the first Dutch fort encountered by traders, a place for provisions and fresh water, and was later listed by UNESCO in 1979."}

{"digest":"Ouagadougou is the capital of Burkina Faso and its cultural and economic centre. Visitors can see the Grand Mosque, the Cathedral built by the French in the 1930s, the National Museum, and the Museum of Music, which displays musical instruments from across Burkina Faso. The city also has parks and gardens such as Bangr Weogo, with walking trails, a small zoo, crocodiles in a marsh, and a pre-colonial sacred forest, plus L'Unité Pédagogique and the Ouaga-Loudun Friendship Garden."}

{"digest":"Nialama Classified Forest, also spelled Nyalama, is a 10,000-hectare forest in the Fouta Djalon highland region of north-west Guinea. Visitors would see hills, cliffs, escarpments, a low-lying plain, seasonal swamps, and a mix of dense gallery forest, open forest, savanna woodland, grassland, and bamboo patches. The forest was surveyed in 1998 and was found to contain four social groups of western chimpanzees, totaling about 83 animals. It is also an Important Bird Area for species including violet turacos and red-throated bee-eaters."}

{"digest":"Labé is a city in Guinea’s Moyenne Guinee region and the regional capital of Fouta Djallon. It has about 59,000 people and is the largest city in its region, as well as the second most populated city in Guinea after Conakry. It lies close to the geographic centre of the country. The passage notes that Fouta Trekking offers all-inclusive trekking through Fouta Djallon, suggesting visitors can use Labé as a base for trekking in the region."}

{"digest":"Boubou Hama National Museum is a museum in Niamey, Niger. The passage focuses on its educational centre, where Harouna Dabougui trained in figurative batik in the late 1970s. Visitors would understand it as a place linked to art teaching and the introduction of batik into Nigerien art education. Dabougui later became the first Nigerien artisan known to teach figurative batik, and his work helped bring the technique into the museum’s educational programme."}

{"digest":"Lake Volta is Ghana’s large artificial reservoir, held behind the Akosombo Dam and spread entirely within the country. A visitor would see a vast lake running from Akosombo in the south to the northern part of Ghana, with islands including Dodi, Dwarf, and Kporve, and Digya National Park on part of the western shore. Its significance is mainly hydroelectric: the dam generates a substantial amount of Ghana’s electricity. The passage also notes it was formed between 1961 and 1965 and was expected to aid fishing."}

{"digest":"Barrakunda Falls, or Barra Kunda Falls, is a waterfall in Senegal’s Tambacounda region on the Gambia River, about 500 kilometres upstream from its mouth. Visitors would see the falls at a point where river travel becomes difficult in the dry season. The passage says the falls were an important milestone and obstacle for European explorers trying to reach the interior. The nearby village of Barrakunda, in the Kingdom of Wuli, sometimes hosted European trading posts from as early as 1651."}

{"digest":"Pendjari National Park is a protected area in north-western Benin, adjoining Arli National Park in Burkina Faso and forming part of the WAP Complex. Visitors would see hills and cliffs of the Atakora range, forest along the Pendjari River, and Sudanian and Guinean savannas with grassland. The park is known for wildlife, including African forest elephants, lions, hippopotamuses, buffalo, and antelopes, and for its rich bird life. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017."}

{"digest":"Despite Automobile Museum is a privately owned automobile museum in East Legon, Accra, Ghana, created from Ghanaian entrepreneur Osei Kwame Despite’s private car collection. Visitors can see more than 80 vehicles, including classic, vintage, luxury and modern performance cars, plus motorcycles. The collection includes models by Bugatti, Rolls-Royce, Bentley, Mercedes-Benz, Jaguar and Harley-Davidson, such as a Rolls-Royce Silver Wraith LWB and several Bentley and Mercedes-Benz vehicles. It is significant as a public display of a personal collection."}

{"digest":"Baleyara is a town in Niger, two hours from Niamey on the route to Filingue. On Sundays, its market draws sellers and buyers from across Niger and nearby countries. Visitors can see one of West Africa’s largest animal markets, with camels, long-horn bulls, horses, sheep, goats, and other livestock for sale. The regular market is lively and reflects Zarma, Bella, and Fulani cultures. Street food, local bread, sweet bread, rice and sauce, and omelet sandwiches are sold nearby."}

{"digest":"Tafawa Balewa Square is a 14.5-hectare ceremonial ground on Lagos Island, Lagos, built on the site of the former Race Course. Visitors would see the entrance sculptures of four white horses and seven red eagles, the Remembrance Arcade for World War I, World War II and Nigerian Civil War victims, and the 26-storey Independence House. The square also has a shopping center, restaurants, parking and a bus terminal, and its cricket oval is regarded as the traditional home of cricket in Nigeria. It has hosted national independence celebrations and other major events."}

{"digest":"Aguégués is a town and commune in southern Benin, made up of lakeside submersible earth islands in the lower Ouémé River. The community is spread along a watery route used by canoes and motorised boats, and the lake area has stilts and wildlife. Visitors can see Goukou and Sohonto Square. The passage also notes the annual Wémèxé festival, an identity festival of the Ouémé department, and that the whole community is flooded each year from July to November."}

{"digest":"Agut Ntswuo, also called Samaru Kataf or Chenkwon, is a town in southern Kaduna State, Nigeria, and one of the largest in Zangon Kataf local government area. It is a junction town linking Kagoro, Zonkwa, and Zangon Kataf. The main people are the Atyap, who speak Tyap, and it is the second largest town in Atyap land. The passage notes its name means a high ground or mound of a shrub, and that nearby places include Kagoro, Zangon Kataf, and Zonkwa."}

{"digest":"The Abdoulaye Faunal Reserve is a protected area in Togo, established in 1951 and covering 300 km2. It is one of several national parks and protected areas created to preserve the country’s biodiversity. The passage does not describe visitor facilities or activities, but it notes the reserve’s significance within Togo’s conservation system. It also says protected areas faced local opposition when established and were later affected by attacks and mass-slaughter of animals during political turmoil in the 1990s."}

{"digest":"Unwana is a town in Afikpo North Local Government Area, Ebonyi State, in south-east Nigeria. The passage says it lies in the Nigerian Equatorial Climate region and has a small annual temperature range, with maximum temperatures between 27 and 38. A visitor would mainly be aware of its climate conditions rather than specific attractions or activities. The passage does not describe sights, landmarks, or things to do there."}

{"digest":"Ussher Fort is a fort in Accra, Ghana, on a rocky point between two lagoons west of the city. Built by the Dutch in 1649 as Fort Crèvecœur, it began as a factory in 1642 and was enlarged by the Dutch West India Company. It was one of three European forts built in the region in the mid-17th century, later transferred to the British in 1868. The fort is significant for its role in European colonial trade and exploitation in Africa and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979."}

{"digest":"The Larabanga Mosque is a small rural mosque in Larabanga, in Ghana’s Savanna Region, and is said to be the oldest mosque in the country and among the oldest in West Africa. Built in Sudanese style from West African adobe, it has two pyramidal towers, timber buttresses, and an east-facing mihrab. Visitors would see the mosque, an old Quran kept there, and a baobab tree next to it said to mark Ayuba’s grave. It is significant for its age, legends, and restoration history."}

{"digest":"Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected wildlife area in Boki Local Government Area of Cross River State, Nigeria. It covers about 100 km² of lowland and submontane rainforest around the Afi Mountains, with rocky peaks reaching about 1,300 metres. Visitors would see forest scenery, birds, and hiking opportunities, and may also visit nearby Drill Ranch. The sanctuary is important for endangered wildlife, especially the Cross River gorilla, Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee and drill, and is listed as an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Juffureh is a small town in The Gambia on the north bank of the Gambia River. It is best known as the reputed origin of Alex Haley’s ancestor Kunta Kinte, described in Roots. Visitors can see the Slave Museum and, across the river, Kunta Kinteh Island. The island is a UNESCO World Heritage Site linked to the West African slave trade, with ruins of British administrative buildings, a small jetty, and skeletal baobab trees remaining after heavy erosion."}

{"digest":"The National Museum of Music, officially the Georges Ouédraogo Museum of Music, is in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, in a renovated two-story building that once housed ADAUA. The building is in Sudanese Sahelian style with dome-shaped roofs and is in the city centre. Visitors would see a growing collection of musical instruments from all families: aerophones, membranophones, idiophones and chordophones. Each object is unique and ranges from 5 to 200 years old."}

{"digest":"Tafi Atome is a small village in Ghana’s Volta Basin, best known for the Tafi Atome Monkey Sanctuary, an ecotourism project centred on mona monkeys. Visitors see monkeys in the surrounding forest and in town, often in the early morning, and can feed them bananas and watch them climb on people. Guided forest tours also show local flora and fauna, and guides can take visitors to the cemetery and the clinic built with tourism funds. The project was created to protect the monkeys and support the local economy."}

{"digest":"Roxa, also called Canhabaque, is an island in the Bissagos Islands of Guinea-Bissau, in the Bolama Region and Bubaque sector. A visitor would see an island that is 20 kilometres long and 11 kilometres wide, with many villages including Ambuduco, Ampucute, Indenazinho and others spread across it. The passage mentions a lighthouse on the east side of the island with a focal height of 26 metres. It also notes a population of 2,478 from the 2009 census."}

{"digest":"Lagoas de Cufada Natural Park is a national park in Guinea-Bissau, covering 890 km2. It was the country’s first protected area and was also designated a Ramsar Wetland. The passage says chimpanzees are reported to live there, nesting in oil palms, though their numbers are unclear. Other wildlife includes hippopotamus, waterbuck, antelope, kob, duikers, African buffalo, colobus monkeys, leopard, hyenas, African manatee, and dwarf crocodile. The park is also an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Fort Witsen, also called Fort Tacaray, was a Dutch fort on the Gold Coast near Takoradi, in present-day Ghana. Established in 1665, it was destroyed after a few years and abandoned in 1684, though a 1791 map shows the Dutch later renewed their presence there. The fort was eventually handed over to Britain in 1872 along with the rest of the Dutch Gold Coast. The passage gives its significance as part of Dutch colonial presence in the region."}

{"digest":"The National Park of Upper Niger is a national park in Guinea, gazetted in January 1997, that protects forest and savannah over a core area of 554 km2. It includes the Mafou Forest, the last remaining dry forest in Guinea and one of the few left in West Africa. Visitors would see savannah, woodland, bushland, and some riparian forest along the Niger and Mafou Rivers. The park is a conservation priority and a Lion Conservation Unit, with farming and sustainable resource use allowed in the buffer zone."}

{"digest":"Freetown is the capital of Sierra Leone, set on a peninsula on the south bank of the Sierra Leone River estuary and facing a major natural harbour. Visitors can see the peninsula mountains and visit beaches such as Lakka Beach, No. 2 River Beach, Bureh and Toke Beach. The city was badly affected by the civil war, then grew rapidly as people moved in from rural areas. Aberdeen district offers a break from the busy city centre, with beach-road stalls selling tourist fare."}

{"digest":"Oye is a town in Ekiti State, Nigeria, and the center of Oye Local Government Area. It was separated from the former Ekiti North Local Government on May 17, 1989, and is surrounded by Ilejemeje, Irepodun/Ifelodun, Ikole, and Ido/Osi local governments. Visitors would mainly be in a town setting rather than at a listed attraction. The passage notes that residents speak the Ekiti dialect and belong to the Ekiti subethnic group, and describes the climate as hot and humid in the dry season and warm, stuffy, and overcast in the wet season."}

{"digest":"The Ghanaian Northern Plain is a region in northern Ghana featuring savannah with baobab trees and villages with distinctive round huts developed over centuries. Visitors can see Nalerigu, the traditional capital of the Mamprusi people, Mole National Park, the country’s largest national park, Sirigu, a scenic village, and the Tongo Hills, a granite mountain range. The area has long been a traditional trade route with Burkina Faso. It is also known for Dagbani and unusual rock formations, including a drum-like rock at Bongo Moon style Landscape."}

{"digest":"John Obey Beach, sometimes shortened to John Obey, is a village in Sierra Leone about 20 miles south of Freetown in the western peninsula region. Visitors can stay in earthbag domes at the beach eco-community and take part in community life, as built through a partnership between the local community and the sustainable tourism organization Tribewanted. The passage says the village had a population of 372 in 2011."}

{"digest":"The Bijagós Islands are an archipelago of about 88 islands and islets off Guinea-Bissau in the Atlantic Ocean. Visitors would see a wide range of ecosystems, including mangroves, palm forests, dry and semi-dry forests, coastal savanna, sand banks, and aquatic zones. The islands support many waterbirds, including migratory waders, gulls, terns, greater flamingos, and pink-backed pelicans. They are also a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and an Important Bird Area. People live on 20 islands year-round, with Bubaque the most populated and Bolama the administrative capital."}

{"digest":"The Aïr and Ténéré Addax Sanctuary is a nature reserve in north-central Niger, within the larger Aïr and Ténéré National Nature Reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It covers part of a vast protected area and was created to protect the critically endangered addax, which once ranged across the Aïr Mountains and Ténéré desert. It is a strict nature reserve, and plans to reintroduce captive-bred addax were interrupted by insurgency and later fighting."}

{"digest":"Nianimaru Forest Park is a forest park in Central River, The Gambia, covering 607 hectares. It was established on January 1, 1954, and sits about four metres above sea level. A visitor would see a forest park in a region where numerous Senegambian stone circles are found, including the stone circles of Niani Maru. The passage gives its significance as part of an area associated with these stone circle sites."}

{"digest":"Mamunta Mayosso Wildlife Sanctuary is a game reserve in Tonkolili District, Northern Province, Sierra Leone, between Magburaka and Yonibana. A visitor would see wildlife including eight primate species, bushbuck, bushpig, genets and duikers, and a wide birdlife record of 252 species. It is one of the few areas in the country protecting the threatened Dwarf Crocodile, and also has Western Chimpanzee, Red Colobus monkey and Pygmy Hippo. The site is important to the local economy and culture and was the first Wildlife Sanctuary managed in Sierra Leone."}

{"digest":"Tanji is a fishing village on the west coast of The Gambia, with about 15,000 people. Visitors can watch the full fishing industry at work, including boat and net making, fish catching, and the salting, smoking, and freezing of fish. The passage notes that fishing boats return home around 17:00. It is also possible to go to the island off the coast from Tanji."}

{"digest":"The Sudanese style mosques in northern Côte d’Ivoire are a group of eight mosques built between the 17th and 19th centuries in a style first brought to the Empire of Mali in the 14th century. The sites include the mosques of Kaouara, Tengréla, Kouto, Nambira, and two mosques in Kong. A visitor would see historic religious buildings across several sub-prefectures in northern Côte d’Ivoire. The collection was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021."}

{"digest":"Tenoumer is a probable impact crater in Mauritania, in the western Sahara Desert. It is nearly circular, about 1.9 km across, and exposed at the surface. The crater rim rises as much as 110 m above the base, while the floor is covered by 200 to 300 m of sediments. It formed in gneiss and granite, with a thin layer of Pliocene sediments. It is significant as a crater now understood to have an impact origin, rather than a volcanic one."}

{"digest":"The Grand Mosque of Ouagadougou is a historic mosque in Burkina Faso’s capital and one of the city’s main Islamic places of worship. Visitors would see a large prayer hall, a central dome, four minarets, two women’s annexes, and a paved courtyard. The mosque was first established in 1952 and later rebuilt between 1973 and 1979. It has been an important center of Muslim religious life, especially for Friday prayers and community organization."}

{"digest":"Chã de Areia is a subdivision of Praia on Santiago Island, Cape Verde, south and west of the city centre. It includes the beach of Gamboa, the old port of Praia, and the Cape Verdean National Archives, which are housed in the former customs building. The annual Festival de Gamboa is held on the beach over three consecutive days in May and is one of the largest music events in Cape Verde."}

{"digest":"Konkouré is a town and sub-prefecture in Mamou Prefecture, Mamou Region, Guinea. The place is tied to the Konkouré River, which rises in west-central Guinea and flows west to the Atlantic; vessels with up to 3 m draft can navigate upstream as far as Konkouré, beyond which there are rapids. The river’s dams supply much of Guinea’s electricity. The estuary and nearby Sangareya Bay are an Important Bird Area with mangroves, mudflats, sandbanks and rice-fields, and support western reef egrets, pied avocets, common redshanks, manatees and bottlenose dolphins."}

{"digest":"Robertsport is a small city in northern Liberia, about 50 km north of Monrovia, known as a surfing destination with some of West Africa’s premier surfing spots. Visitors would see a town still recovering from two civil wars, with many plantation-style houses in disrepair after repeated looting. The passage also notes its significance as a place that should be a popular destination because of its surfing, despite the city’s recent history and damaged buildings."}

{"digest":"Pama Reserve is a partial reserve in Kompienga Province, Burkina Faso, established in 1955 and covering 2,237 km2. Its boundaries include the Singou River to the east, National Road N18 to the west, and the Pendjari River on the southern border with Benin. A visitor would know it as wildlife habitat for elephants, hippopotamuses, lions, and leopards, as well as for 450 species of flowering plants."}

{"digest":"Lejja is a community of 33 villages in Enugu State, southeastern Nigeria, inhabited mainly by the Igbo people. Visitors would see a landscape of hills and valleys on the edge of the Benue Plateau, and could visit Otobo Ugwu square in Dunoka village, a famous iron smelting site with more than 800 cylindrical slag blocks. Archaeological finds include ironmaking, residential and ritual sites. Lejja is significant as one of the earliest and most important iron smelting sites in sub-Saharan Africa, dating to 2000 BC."}

{"digest":"Forte de São João Baptista de Ajudá is a small restored fort in Ouidah, Benin. Built in 1721, it was the last of three European forts there used to tap the slave trade of the Slave Coast. After the slave trade was legally abolished, it was mostly abandoned, then permanently reoccupied in 1865. It later became an international oddity when Portuguese sovereignty was kept over a tiny enclave surrounded by French territory. Today, the restored fort is part of the Ouidah Museum of History."}

{"digest":"Djado is a commune and ghost town in the Bilma department of Niger, on the Djado plateau in the northeastern Ténéré Desert. Visitors would see the ruins of the former settlement on rocky cliffs, with subterranean ponds below, and could reach the Kaouar valley from the cliffs; pebbly desert lies to the west. The commune also includes the villages of Chirfa, Séguédine, and Yaba. The passage says Djado was once part of Kanem-Bornu, was later raided, and was largely abandoned after people moved to Kaouar."}

{"digest":"Ibeku is a town in Abia State, south east Nigeria, and the administrative headquarters of Umuahia North. It lies in the hilly terrain of Umuahia and is part of a chiefdom in the southeastern region. Visitors would mainly observe the town’s setting and its tropical rainforest climate, with high humidity, high temperatures, and considerable rainfall for most of the year. The people of Ibeku speak Igbo, and the passage identifies it as a local administrative centre."}

{"digest":"Gwadabawa is a town and Local Government Area in Sokoto State, northwestern Nigeria, serving as the LGA headquarters. It lies in the dry Sahel zone and is part of the historic Sokoto region, known for Islamic scholarship, Hausa and Fulani culture, and traditional institutions. A visitor would mainly encounter a very hot environment, a long dry season, and local farming and livestock activities. People there grow millet, sorghum, groundnut, and onions."}

{"digest":"Mole National Park is Ghana’s largest wildlife refuge and one of the country’s seven national parks. It lies in the Savannah Region on undisturbed Guinea savannah, reached via Larabanga, not far from Damongo. Visitors would see savanna and riparian ecosystems, the Levi and Mole Rivers, and drinking holes left in the dry season. The park is significant as a wildlife refuge set aside in 1958, a national park from 1971, and an important study area for scientists, with resident elephants and antelope species."}

{"digest":"Assagny National Park is a national park in southern Côte d'Ivoire, on the coast west of Abidjan between the Bandama River and Ébrié Lagoon. Visitors would see a broad, often waterlogged basin with swamps of mangroves, some moist forest and coastal savanna, crossed by the navigable Asagni Canal. Wildlife includes elephants, chimpanzees, monkeys, bushpigs, African forest buffalos, crocodiles and manatees, plus wetland birds. It was recognized as a Ramsar site in 2005 and as an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Wa Naa’s Palace is the home of the King of the Wala people in Wa, in Ghana’s Upper West Region, and sits in the heart of town. Visitors would see a traditional mud-brick palace built in Sudano-Sahelian style, with Y-shaped wooden columns and flat roofs. The chief sits on a lion or antelope skin, while others sit on cow or sheep skin. The palace is important culturally, politically, religiously, and socially, and it also serves as the burial place for former kings."}

{"digest":"Ervatão, or Porto de Ervatão, is a beach on the southeast coast of Boa Vista in Cape Verde, between the headlands Ponta de Ervatão and Ponta Cosme. It lies within the Turtle Nature Reserve. The passage says the area receives 70% of all turtles nesting on Boa Vista, and that 8,000 turtle nests were counted there in July 2009. A visitor would see the beach and the protected nesting area."}

{"digest":"Terras Salgadas, meaning “salty lands,” is a vast natural area in the northwestern part of Maio, Cape Verde, within Parque Natural do Norte da Ilha do Maio. It is the largest saline ecosystem in the archipelago and is marked by imposing sand dunes. Visitors would see an area rich in endemic sea birds, fish, and sea turtles. The nearest settlements are Morrinho, Cascabulho, and Santo António. It was mentioned on a 1747 map by Jacques-Nicolas Bellin."}

{"digest":"The Oba of Lagos, also called the Eleko of Eko, is the traditional Yoruba ruler of Lagos. The role is ceremonial and has no political power, but the Oba is still sought as a counsellor or sponsor by politicians and appears in tourism advertisements for the city. The passage traces the title’s lineage to Ashipa, an Awori war captain of the Oba of Benin, and notes that the last tribute links to Benin ended after the 1851 defeat of Oba Kosoko."}

{"digest":"Marendet is a village and archaeological site in central Niger, within the Aderbissinat commune. The site was an important stop on a 9th and 10th century trade route linking Wagadu to Egypt through Gao, and it was also a source of copper. A visitor would see an archaeological site, though the passage notes it is now threatened by erosion and looting. Marendet is part of the Sahel region, where people traditionally raise goats, camels, and cattle."}

{"digest":"Savannah Region is a region in the Ghanaian Northern Plains and one of Ghana’s newest and largest regions. Its vegetation is characterised by savannah. Visitors can go to Mole National Park, described as the largest national park in the country. The region lies in the north of Ghana and its capital is Damongo. The passage also notes that the region was created after a petition and referendum, with the new region formally launched in 2019."}

{"digest":"The Monument du 22 Novembre 1970 is a monument in Conakry, Guinea, built in memory of the victims of the 1970 coup attempt known as Operation Green Sea. It commemorates the failed invasion of Conakry by Portuguese troops and Guinean fighters, which captured Camp Boiro and briefly took General Lansana Diané. A visitor would see the monument and its inscription, which declares that the revolution is imperative and that imperialism finds its grave in Guinea."}

{"digest":"The Saloum Delta, or Sine-Saloum Delta, is a river delta in Senegal where the Saloum River enters the North Atlantic Ocean. It includes brackish channels, more than 200 islands and islets, mangrove forest, an Atlantic marine environment, and dry forest. Visitors would find Saloum Delta National Park and see birdlife such as flamingos, herons, terns, and spoonbills. The delta is significant as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and for shellfish mounds and burial-ground artefacts that shed light on human occupation."}

{"digest":"Crispina Peres was a woman trader based in Cacheu, then part of the West African slave trade network. Born in Geba around 1615, she belonged to a lineage of African women traders active in ports such as Guinguim, Farim, Cacheu and Geba. She exchanged European goods for human beings, linking local and regional trade routes to the Atlantic World. Through her connections, she controlled trade between Portuguese traders and indigenous African rulers and acted as a diplomatic mediator."}

{"digest":"Aflao is a coastal town in Ghana on the border with Togo. It is described as a typical African border town built to service the movement of people and goods. A visitor would see a few restaurants and hotels, and much of the local economy is based on street-side currency converters exchanging Ghanaian cedis for Togolese West African francs."}

{"digest":"Nyanya is a suburban district in Abuja Municipal Area Council, linking nearby Nasarawa State to Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory. It is generally regarded as part of the Abuja metropolis and is growing as a residential area for low- and medium-income earners. Visitors would see a multicultural neighbourhood where English is most commonly spoken, alongside Hausa, and a concentration of government institutions. The passage also mentions Government Secondary School Nyanya."}

{"digest":"Lake Chad is a freshwater lake at the junction of Nigeria, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon. It is an important wetland ecosystem and one of Africa’s major freshwater fish-producing areas. A visitor would see a lake with deeper southern parts and shallower northern parts, whose water level and size change greatly with the seasons. The passage says the lake is rich in aquatic resources and notes its long history, including the larger ancient “Mega-Chad,” and that lakeside fishermen’s settlements and agriculture emerged around it."}

{"digest":"Harper is a city in southern Liberia and the former capital of Maryland. It lies in the southeast of the country. A visitor would see its beaches and beach houses, though the houses are now dilapidated. Even so, they still give a sense of the place’s former glory. The passage also names Stone Mason Building in Upcape and Cape Palmas Beach near the port."}

{"digest":"The Ghanaian Coastal Plain is a region of Ghana known for its coastline, forts, castles, beaches, and historic slave sites. Visitors can see Elmina and Cape Coast forts, including Cape Coast Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, as well as Fort San Sebastian in Shama and other listed forts. The area also offers Axim’s fort and beaches, Kokrobite beach, Tema’s fish market, Ada Foah’s wetland for bird and turtle watching, Nzulezo stilt village, Kakum National Park’s canopy walkway, and Shai Hills wildlife."}

{"digest":"Caravela is the northernmost island of the Bissagos Islands of Guinea-Bissau and part of the Sector of Caravela, which also includes Carache, Maio, Ponta and Formosa. A visitor would see a heavily forested island with mangroves and white sandy beaches. The island has a small airfield. The passage gives its size and population, noting 907 people on the island in the 2009 census and 4,263 in the sector."}

{"digest":"Abuko National Park is a nature reserve south of the town of Abuko in The Gambia and the country’s first designated wildlife reserve. Visitors would see savanna and gallery forest with trees such as oil palm, mahogany, iroko and Anthocleista procera, plus wildlife including three monkey species, antelope, squirrels, porcupines, civets, mongooses, galagos and rodents. The park also has reptile species, an animal orphanage with a pack of hyenas, and more than 270 bird species. It is designated an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Sidi Yahya Mosque is a mosque and madrasa in Timbuktu, Mali, also known as the Mosque of Muhammad-n-Allah. Begun in 1400 and finished in 1440, it is one of Timbuktu’s oldest mosques and was later rebuilt in 1939. Visitors would see its modern appearance and the mosque associated with the scholarly community once called the “University of Timbuktu.” It contains the tomb of its first imam, Sidi Yahya al-Tadelsi, and parts were destroyed in 2012 and later reconstructed."}

{"digest":"Biseni Forest is a 219-square-kilometre freshwater swamp forest in the Taylor Creek floodplain of the Niger Delta, northwest of Ahoada and west of Upper Orashi Forest. Visitors would see a swampy woodland that can dry in the dry season and turn into a flooded forest after heavy rains, with raffia palms, woody broadleaved trees, and tall grass swamps near river channels. It is also a birdwatching site with records of migratory and aquatic birds."}

{"digest":"Carache is an island in the northwestern Bissagos Islands of Guinea-Bissau, in the Bolama Region and the sector of Caravela. It is separated from Caravela by a narrow channel. The island is 18.7 km long, up to 7.3 km wide, and had a population of 428 in the 2009 census. Its largest villages are Binte and Ampintcha. The passage gives no specific visitor activities on Carache itself, but nearby Keré offers fishing trips and visits to villages in Caravela and Carache."}

{"digest":"Ouadane, or Wādān, is a small desert town in central Mauritania on the southern edge of the Adrar Plateau. Visitors can see the old town, a World Heritage Site, which is still substantially intact though in ruins, and a small modern settlement outside its gate. The town was a staging post for trans-Saharan trade and caravans carrying salt from the Idjil mines. It is also the nearest town to the Richat Structure. Historical accounts describe it as an important Adrar town and an entrepôt for salt trade."}

{"digest":"Timbuktu is a city in Mali, about 20 kilometres north of the Niger River, and the capital of the Tombouctou Region. A visitor would see a place long linked to Saharan trade and Islamic scholarship, once enriched by salt, gold, and ivory routes and by the Sankoré Madrasah, an Islamic university. The passage says it became a major scholarly and cultural centre, known for its book trade. It also notes recent threats to cultural sites and preservation efforts."}

{"digest":"Mare d'Oursi is a small, shallow lake in Oudalan Province in northern Burkina Faso, near the town of Oursi. It lies within the Sylvo-Pastoral and Partial Faunal Reserve of the Sahel, the country's largest protected area. Visitors would see one of the temporary lakes in the reserve, which is important for migratory birds. The lake is also listed as a Ramsar wetland of international importance."}

{"digest":"Santa Maria salt ponds, or Salinas de Santa Maria, are a protected complex of salt evaporation ponds north of Santa Maria on the island of Sal, Cape Verde. A visitor would see the ponds set within a 69-hectare protected landscape. The passage says the town was founded in 1830 for salt production, once shipping up to 30,000 tons a year. The ponds are significant as the site of a long salt-export industry that declined after 1887 and ended in 1984."}

{"digest":"Kédougou is a town on the Gambia River in the hills of Bassari country, and the capital of its administrative region in southeastern Senegal. It is the largest city in Southeastern Senegal, noted for its rainy, hilly landscape and a culture described as more Guinean than Senegalese. Visitors can see mountains and waterfalls, including Dindefelo Falls, a 50-100 m waterfall in a lush forest, and Niokolo-Koba National Park. It is described as a center for eco-tourism."}

{"digest":"The Bura archaeological site is in the Tillabéry Region, Tera Department, southwest Niger. It gave its name to the first-millennium Bura culture. Visitors would see a large necropolis area with burial mounds, religious altars, ancient dwellings, and coffins topped with distinctive terra cotta statuettes. The site has produced large terracotta burial jars, funerary pottery, and the oldest equestrian clay statues from Bura sites in the Niger River valley. It is significant for its archaeological remains and as the source of the Bura name."}

{"digest":"Sal is an island of Cape Verde. Most tourists stay in Santa Maria at the southern end, about 20 minutes from the airport and Espargos. Visitors see beaches, restaurants, bars, hotels, a lively pedestrian street, the pier and the town square. The eastern end has a small beach and is a centre for surfing and windsurfing, while the western end has larger hotels and Ponta Preta’s dunes and beach. Elsewhere, Palmeira is the main port, and Pedra de Lume is near the old Salinas, a candidate world heritage site."}

{"digest":"The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15 is a Soviet single-seat transonic jet fighter aircraft. It was one of the first successful jet fighters with swept wings and was built to fly near Mach 1. The passage says it outclassed straight-winged jet fighters in the Korean War, prompting the United States Air Force to rush the F-86 Sabre to Korea. It is also described as one of the most produced jet aircraft, with more than 13,000 manufactured, and it remains in service with the Korean People's Army Air Force as an advanced trainer."}

{"digest":"Abengourou is a city in eastern Côte d'Ivoire with about 120,000 inhabitants. It is the administrative capital of the Moyen-Comoé region and a centre for trade, learning, medical care and religion. Visitors can see the Cathedral of St. Theresa of the Child Jesus, seat of the Diocese of Abengourou, and the residence of the Anyi paramount chief, whose 1882 mansion is extensively decorated with artefacts. The surrounding fertile forest area produces cacao and coffee that are brought to Abengourou for onward shipment."}

{"digest":"Apapa Amusement Park is an amusement park in Lagos, Nigeria. Visitors can walk through its Arabian-style buildings, with flat rooftops, dark yellow hues, and rough-hewn walls, and use the park’s various games and facilities. The park began operating in 1976 as Lagos Lunar Park, was demolished in 2012 because of environmental concerns, then rebuilt and reopened after a makeover and maintenance. It is a partnership between the Lagos State government and Crystal Cubes Construction Company."}

{"digest":"Muso Kunda Museum of Women is a museum in Bamako, founded in 1995 by Malian feminist and historian Adame Ba Konaré. It is dedicated to promoting women’s rights, breaking stereotypes, and recording women’s memory. Visitors can see portraits of women heroes from the March 1991 revolution, a traditional costume gallery, and mannequins displaying traditional and modern women’s clothing from different regions of Mali. The museum also shows women’s roles in politics, development, national movements, and daily life, including tools used at home and how they have changed with technology."}

{"digest":"The Mobee Royal Family Slave Relics Museum in Badagry, Lagos State, Nigeria, is a privately owned museum run by descendants of the traditional rulers of Badagry. It displays relics of the slave trade, including manacles used to shackle enslaved people, a late-18th-century branding tool belonging to slave merchant Sunbu Mobee, and a ring-shaped punishment tool. The museum also contains Mobee’s grave, and outside are two 18th-century cannons that were reportedly traded for slaves."}

{"digest":"Volta Delta is the central region of Burkina Faso. In Ouagadougou, visitors can see several museums, including the National Museum with exhibits on local cultures, and attend the Moro Naaba ceremony held every Friday morning. The city also hosts FESPACO, a film festival for African filmmakers. In Koudougou, there is the Royal Palace of Issouka, an example of earthen architecture, and the annual NAK cultural week. Pô serves as access to Kaboré-Tambi National Park, the Nazinga ranch, and Gourounsi country."}

{"digest":"The World War Cenotaph in Lokoja is a war memorial for fallen British and Nigerian officers and other ranks who died in the world wars. Visitors would see a large concrete block with old artillery mounted on it, with light cannons and machine guns on small pavements, plus relics of weapons and plaques inscribed with names of military personnel. It is in Lokoja’s colonial administrative area and is used for yearly army remembrance ceremonies in Kogi State."}

{"digest":"Fort Apollonia is a fort in Beyin, Ghana, originally linked to Portuguese naming and later used by the Swedes, British, Dutch, and British again. A visitor would see a restored fort that has housed the Museum of Nzema Culture and History since 2010. The passage says it was rehabilitated in 1962 and completed in 1968. It is significant for its role in European colonial history and as testimony to the Atlantic slave trade; it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979."}

{"digest":"Guinee Maritime is the coastal region of Guinea, covering all of Kindia province and the southern part of Boke province. A visitor can see Conakry’s national museum, botanical gardens, and the Grand Mosque, or go to the Loos Islands, three islands near Conakry. Kindia is described as the city of citrus fruits. The region is a gentle coastal plain with the Fouta Djallon plateau rising behind it, and it is the home of the Susu people and their culture."}

{"digest":"Fort D’El Rei, also called Mindelo Fort, is in Mindelo on São Vicente, Cape Verde. Built in 1852–1853, it is the oldest construction in the city and was made to defend Porto Grande harbour. The square, single-storey fortlet has a central courtyard and wide views over the city and bay. It later housed the port’s signal station and served as a civil jail from 1930 to 1970. As of 2012, it was in ruins."}

{"digest":"Karaga is the capital of Karaga District in Ghana’s Volta Basin region and a small Dagomba farming town about 60km northeast of Tamale. It is known as a gateway to eastern Dagbon and as one of the traditional paramount chieftaincies of the Dagbon Kingdom. Visitors can see a large mud-brick chief’s palace, a busy periodic market, and nearby rural villages. The town’s history is tied to agriculture, trade routes, and Dagomba warrior traditions, and festivals may include drumming, dancing, horse riding, and warrior displays."}

{"digest":"Fortim d'El-Rei is a fort in Mindelo, on São Vicente in Cape Verde, located on a hill north of the city centre in the Fortinho neighbourhood. Built in 1852, it was intended to defend Porto Grande Bay and the city of Mindelo. Since 1930 it has been used only for civil purposes and gradually fell into disrepair. A visitor would see the fortress site above the city; the surrounding subdivision of Fortinho takes its name from it."}

{"digest":"Tagbo Falls is a waterfall near Mount Afadjato at Liati Wote, about 27 kilometres east of Hohoe in Ghana’s Volta Region. The water drops in several stages, with the final fall about 60 metres high, and the area is surrounded by rainforest. Visitors would see the waterfall and its forest setting. The passage identifies it as one of the waterfalls in the Volta Region of Ghana."}

{"digest":"Baía is a settlement in the eastern part of Santiago, Cape Verde, in the municipality of São Domingos. It lies near the east coast, about 14 km northeast of Praia, and includes localities such as Achada Baixo, Castelinho and Covão Santana. A visitor would see the ruined Gothic church of Nossa Senhora da Luz on the shore near Baía. The passage says this church was part of the 15th-century Portuguese settlement of Alcatrazes, giving the place historical significance."}

{"digest":"Cruzinha is a village in northern Santo Antão, Cape Verde, and the name of a protected nature reserve on the island’s north coast between the Ribeira da Garça and Ribeira do Mocho rivers. The reserve contains Santo Antão’s only coastal dunes. Visitors can use the village as a starting point for coastal hiking, including the route between Cruzinha and Ponta do Sol, a moderate 5–6 hour walk with steep sections and about 200 metres of elevation change."}

{"digest":"Ẹgbẹ Mẹkun, popularly called Ẹgbẹ, is a historic ancient town in Yagba West Local Government Area of Kogi State, Nigeria, bordering Kogi and Kwara States. A visitor would see undulating hills covered with luxuriant savannah vegetation around the town. The passage says this landscape is why it is sometimes called “Jerusalem in Nigeria.” The people speak Yagba, and the town’s ancestry is linked to the Yorubas in Nigeria."}

{"digest":"Ojuelegba is a suburb in Surulere local government area of Lagos State, South West Nigeria. It is regarded as one of the busiest places in Lagos and is known for its crowded setting. A visitor would mainly see a busy transport point linking Lagos Mainland and the Island, and serving commuters to Yaba, Mushin and Surulere. The area has also been depicted in music, including Fela’s Confusion album and songs by Wizkid and Oritse Femi. Its past nightlife linked revelers to Moshalashi Shrine and nearby redlight streets."}

{"digest":"Birnin Kudu is a town in Jigawa State, Nigeria, about 120 km southeast of Kano. Visitors can see ancient rock paintings and gongs at the Birnin Kudu Rock Paintings, evidence of a civilization over two millennia old. The town is also a market hub for agricultural products such as peanuts and millet. It is home to the historic Government College, which has produced several prominent leaders."}

{"digest":"The Mabi/Yaya Classified Forest in Ivory Coast covers 294 km2 and lies near Kossandji and the western edge of Annépé. A visitor would be looking at a protected forest reserve, classified as IUCN category IV. Its significance is ecological: BirdLife International has designated it an Important Bird Area because it supports many bird species, including the white-breasted guineafowl, and it is one of the last habitats of the forest toad Sclerophrys togoensis."}

{"digest":"Shama is a coastal town in Ghana’s Shama district, on the Ghanaian Coastal Plain. Visitors would see the ocean from most parts of town, along with lush beaches and vegetation. The town is near Takoradi and Ivoiro, the border town between Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Shama is also home to Fort St. Sebastian, also called Fort São Sebastião de Xama. Built by the Portuguese, it is Ghana’s third oldest fort and a UNESCO World Heritage Site."}

{"digest":"Monte Gordo Natural Park is a protected mountain area on São Nicolau, Cape Verde, centred on Monte Gordo, the island’s highest point at 1,312 m. Visitors would see a humid mountain landscape with forested higher slopes, frequent mist, and trees thickly covered with lichens. The park preserves some of Cape Verde’s original vegetation, including Pinus, Eucalyptus and Cupressus forests, as well as endemic plants and wildlife such as the São Nicolau skink, Cape Verde wall gecko, Fea’s petrel and Cape Verde warbler. It is also an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"The African Renaissance Monument is a 50-metre bronze statue on one of the Collines des Mamelles hills outside Dakar, overlooking the Atlantic Ocean in the Ouakam suburb. A visitor would see a family figure reaching upward, with a man carrying a child and holding his wife. It was launched by President Abdoulaye Wade, designed by Pierre Goudiaby Atepa, and dedicated on 4 April 2010, Senegal’s National Day. It is the tallest statue in Africa and represents African rebirth and moving forward."}

{"digest":"Masjid Al-Noor, also called the Al-Noor Mosque or “The Light” mosque, is a mosque complex in Wayamba in Ghana’s Northern Region. A visitor would see a 6,000-seater complex with a school, library, dormitories, workers’ and guest residences, a clinic with pharmacy, offices, the Sheikh Adam Issah Centre for Islamic Research, and zakat, education and scholarship funds. It was commissioned by Mohammed Amin Adam and inaugurated by Osman Nuhu Sharubutu and Mahamudu Bawumia."}

{"digest":"Dalaba is a town in Guinea’s Fouta Djallon, in the Moyenne Guinea region and the highest town in the country, at about 1,300 metres. Visitors can hike, visit viewpoints over the city centre and nearby hills, and see notable buildings such as Case a Palabres, a circular Fulani-style structure with interior mosaics, and Villa Sili, the former residence of the French governor. Nearby are Chutes de Ditinn, a waterfall dropping from a cliff, and the natural bridge Le Pont De Dieu. Miriam Makeba lived here in exile."}

{"digest":"Morro de Areia Nature Reserve is a protected area on the southwestern coast of Boa Vista in Cape Verde, named for the 167 m Morro de Areia hill. It stretches from Praia de Chaves to Praia de Santa Monica and includes a 300 m-wide marine protection zone. Visitors would see coastal dunes and the protected shoreline. The reserve was established to protect dune sand dynamics and endemic wildlife, including red-billed tropicbirds, ospreys, turtles, nurse sharks, and numerous invertebrates."}

{"digest":"Grand-Bassam is a town in southeastern Ivory Coast east of Abidjan, split by the Ébrié Lagoon into Ancien Bassam and Nouveau Bassam. Visitors can see the former French settlement, with restored colonial buildings, a cathedral, and the Ivory Coast National Museum of Costume in the former Governor’s Palace, while the inland side is the main commercial centre. Its historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its colonial architecture, town-planning, and its juxtaposition with a traditional Nzema village."}

{"digest":"Kofar Mata is a city gate area in Kano, Nigeria, near the historic Kano city walls. It is home to the Kofar Mata Dye Pits, a group of traditional indigo dyeing pits that have operated for centuries. Visitors would see deep circular vats used for hand-dyeing textiles with natural indigo, where cloth is dipped and exposed to air to turn deep blue. The site is closely tied to the cultural and economic history of the Hausa people and is regarded as a symbol of Kano’s heritage."}

{"digest":"Bani is a town in northern Burkina Faso known for its seven clay mosques. Built starting in 1978 under the leadership of the Prophet of Bani, Mohamed el-Hajj, six mosques stand atop a hill facing the grand mosque in the centre of town. Visitors can see their weathered, older appearance from lack of maintenance. The passage says the mosques made Bani a tourist draw, though visitors may encounter many children asking for donations and gifts."}

{"digest":"Elmina is a city in Ghana’s Coastal Plain region. Its name comes from the Portuguese word for “Mine,” linked to the gold that gave rise to the name Gold Coast. Visitors can see Elmina Castle, built in 1482 and described as the oldest European structure in Africa and the oldest slave fort. The castle tour includes the “room of no return,” slave dungeons, a museum, restaurant, bookstore, and gift shop. Nearby Fort St. Jago is part of a World Heritage site."}

{"digest":"Gaoua is a market town in Burkina Faso’s Black Volta Region and a hilly city in the southwest, about 60 km from Côte d’Ivoire and roughly 50 km from Ghana. It is known as the home of the Lobi people, along with Dagara, Birifor, Jula, Dogose, Gan, and Gwan communities. Visitors can see Lobi “villages,” which are actually mini-fortresses scattered around the countryside, drink chapolo in a cabaret, and book trips through the museum to outlying villages known for basket weaving and pottery."}

{"digest":"Koutammakou, or Batammariba Country, is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in northern Togo near the border with Benin. It is a largely rural area with no major cities, known for the Batammariba people, their traditional mud tower-houses called takienta, and spiritual customs that have remained largely unchanged for centuries. Visitors would see fortified clay houses, sacrificial altars outside them, and villages in areas such as Nadoba, the Niamtougou Corridor, and borderland settlements."}

{"digest":"Efon-Alaaye is a town in Ekiti State, mainly inhabited by Yoruba people. It has about 280,000 people, and farming is the main occupation. The town has many hills and rough terrain, so visitors can do hill-climbing and sightseeing of the surroundings. A key place to visit is the Alaaye of Efon-Alaaye Palace, the palace of the town’s king, which contains tourist attractions."}

{"digest":"Bubaque is an island in Guinea-Bissau’s Bijagós Islands, and also the name of its main town. Visitors would see a heavily forested island known for wildlife, along with the headquarters of the UNESCO nature reserve and a museum. The island is 75 km2, with the town of Bubaque as its main settlement. Travel on the island is by motorbike or on foot, and there is a port with a weekly ferry to Bissau and an airport serving the island."}

{"digest":"Outamba-Kilimi National Park is in Karene District, north-west Sierra Leone, near Guinea. It has two parts, Outamba and Kilimi, with flat terrain, hills, rivers, and vegetation of gallery forest, woodland, grassland, savanna, and swamp forest. Visitors can see western chimpanzees, colobus monkeys, sooty mangabeys, hippos, pygmy hippos, forest elephants, warthogs, bongo antelopes, and many birds. The park was first set aside to protect chimpanzees and is an Important Bird Area. Susu people live in and around it, and simple huts are available for visitors."}

{"digest":"Bao Bolong Wetland Reserve is a protected wetland area in The Gambia on the north bank of the River Gambia, extending toward the Senegalese border along the Bao Bolon tributary. It covers a large estuary system, including the Bao Bolong river and several smaller bolongs, with dense mangrove forest along the river. The reserve was first declared in 1993 and expanded in 1996. It was the first reserve in The Gambia recognized under the Ramsar Convention for protecting water-bird habitat."}

{"digest":"Samuel Sidibé is the director of the National Museum of Mali. The passage says a visitor would not be seeing a place itself here, but that in 2006 he signed a collaboration agreement with the Aga Khan Trust for Culture. That agreement gave the museum a new information technology system and improved conservation facilities for its collections, building on earlier cooperation on the conservation of earth architecture. He is also noted for awards and academic credentials, including the Prince Claus Prize."}

{"digest":"Ayorou is a riverside town in southwestern Niger, about three hours from Niamey. Visitors usually go for the colorful Sunday market, either as a day trip or overnight stay. At the market, people can wander among goods not available in Niamey or elsewhere and see a mix of cultures. The passage says the atmosphere is calmer and more polite than in other markets. Food is mainly street food, with one bar/restaurant in town and local sugary drinks sold on the street."}

{"digest":"Krokosua Hills Forest Reserve is a 481 km2 forest reserve in Ghana, established in 1935. A visitor would see a heavily logged forest, with evidence of logging in progress and high levels of hunting activity noted in field surveys. The passage also says chimpanzee presence was reported by hunters, though surveys found no evidence of chimpanzees at the site. It is significant as one of Ghana’s forest reserves and as a place surveyed for chimpanzee abundance and signs of human impact."}

{"digest":"Cova is a volcanic caldera in east-central Santo Antão, Cape Verde, within Cova-Paul-Ribeira da Torre Natural Park. A visitor would see a crater about 1 km across, with walls rising to about 1,500 m and a small village inside the crater, part of Cabo da Ribeira. The bottom is used to grow maize and beans, while the crater walls have natural vegetation and, on the south side, forests of Pinus and Cupressus. The formation dates from between 1.4 million and 700,000 years ago."}

{"digest":"Baía da Murdeira is a wide crescent-shaped bay on the southwest coast of Sal in Cape Verde, named for the village of Murdeira on its shore. At its northwestern end are the steep cliff of Rabo de Junco and the nearby uninhabited Ilhéu Rabo de Junco islet. The bay is a marine nature reserve covering land and sea, including the islet. It is significant as a nesting area for sea turtles and seabirds."}

{"digest":"Fort Frederiksborg, later called Fort Royal, was a Danish-Norwegian and later English fort on the Gold Coast in present-day Ghana, built in 1661 on Amanfro Hill near Cape Coast Castle. A visitor would see the remains of a small fort that once overlooked and could bombard the nearby castle. It briefly served as headquarters of the Danish West India Company, was later pawned and sold to the English, rebuilt in 1699, and then abandoned. It is significant as part of a World Heritage site for its testimony to European economic influence and the Atlantic slave trade."}

{"digest":"Kusum Forest Park is a forest park in eastern Gambia, in Kantora district of the Upper River Region. Established in 1954, it covers 316 hectares. The park lies between Garowol to the west and the Gambia River to the east. The passage gives its significance mainly as a designated forest park and identifies its location and size, but it does not describe specific visitor activities or features inside the park."}

{"digest":"The Kpalimé War Memorial is a memorial at the entrance to Kpalimé in Togo’s Plateaux Region, set in a public square. It commemorates people considered to have contributed to the defence of the territory and to Togolese independence. The monument has three large curved arms covered with stones from the Kloto Mountains, especially Akata, known locally as Akatakpé. Visitors would see a place used for remembrance, wreath-laying ceremonies on Martyrs’ Day, and commemorations linked to the 1986 attack against Togo."}

{"digest":"Diawling National Park is a protected area in south-west Mauritania near the Senegal River delta, covering 16,000 hectares of former floodplain. A visitor would see a wetland landscape that becomes large lakes in the rainy season, with many birds and fish. The park is known for over 220 identified bird species, including flamingos, pelicans, spoonbills and terns, and it is an Important Bird Area and part of a Trans-Border Biosphere Reserve. Its wildlife sanctuary status reflects its significance."}

{"digest":"The ruins of Loropéni are a medieval heritage site near Loropéni in southern Burkina Faso and the country’s first UNESCO World Heritage site, listed in 2009. The site contains stone walls from a medieval fortress, considered the best preserved of ten in the area. The ruins date back at least a thousand years and were occupied by the Lohron or Kulango people. They prospered through the trans-Saharan gold trade, then were abandoned in the early 19th century. The site is overgrown and partly hard to see."}

{"digest":"Boti Falls is a twin waterfall in Boti, Yilo Krobo District, in Ghana’s Eastern Region, in the Huhunya forest reserve. It is fed by the Ponmpon River and drops about 30 metres into a pool, where locals swim. At high flow, the two side-by-side falls merge, and visitors can stand at the bottom of 250 concrete steps and be surrounded by falling water in a canyon. Local myth says the larger fall is male, the smaller female, and their merging can form a rainbow."}

{"digest":"Beri Kolon Forest Park, also called Berikolon, is a forest park in The Gambia covering 1,052 hectares.
