It is in the Lower River Region, across Jarra Central District and Jarra East District, on the north side of South Bank Road. A visitor would see a large forest area beside the country’s main trunk road, around 15 miles east of Soma. The passage also notes that it was established on January 1, 1954."}

{"digest":"Kasewe Forest Reserve is an area of hills in Moyamba District, Sierra Leone, near Lunsar. Designated as a forest reserve, it covers 1.224 km2 and includes moist semi-deciduous and evergreen forests on volcanic rock hills about 500m above the interior plains. The passage says a visitor would see forested hills, but notes there is little credible biodiversity data. It is believed to shelter a significant number of endangered mammal species, while the reserve is also affected by severe deforestation."}

{"digest":"Diéfoula Forest is a protected forest in Comoé Province in western Burkina Faso, near the border with Ivory Coast. A visitor would be in a protected area that has been merged with Logoniégué Forest into the Forêt Classée et Réserve Partielle de Faune de la Comoé-Léraba. It is part of a connected cross-border protected area with the Ivorian Warigué protected area and Comoé National Park. The forest contains white-naped mangabeys and dominant trees including Daniellia olivieri, Isoberlinia doka, Pterocarpus erinaceus and Khaya senegalensis."}

{"digest":"The Alexandre Sènou Adandé Ethnographic Museum is an ethnographic museum in Porto-Novo, Benin. It was established in 1957 by the Dahomey Institute and is operated by Alexandre Sènou Adandé, a noted ethnologist who served as chief archivist and librarian at the Institut Fondamental d'Afrique Noire in Dakar from 1948 to 1960."}

{"digest":"Atar is a town of about 25,000 people in Saharan Mauritania and a base for exploring the Adrar region. Visitors can use it to arrange day trips to nearby oases, dunes, and old towns such as Terjit, Mhaireth, Valle Blanche, Amatlich, Azougi, and Chinguetti, by bush taxi, 4x4, or bike. The town has a few markets with lower prices than Chinguetti, and bargaining is expected. Its Atar Mosque, dating from 1674, is one of the oldest mosques in the country."}

{"digest":"Bole Mosque is in the center of Bole in Ghana’s Savannah Region. Visitors would see an adobe mosque built in the Sudano-Sahelian style, with sticks and mud, short towers, and wooden poles set between the buttresses for maintenance work such as painting and plastering. The passage says the mosque collapsed in 2023 after heavy rain and termite damage, then was rebuilt in early 2024 with traditional materials. Its construction date is unknown, though it is dated to the 17th century and linked in oral tradition to the 18th century."}

{"digest":"Lomé is the capital and largest city of Togo, and its economic and cultural center. Founded in the 19th century by Ewe people, it grew into a major port, trading and administrative center, and later became the capital of German Togoland and then remained the capital under French rule and after independence. Visitors can enjoy beaches, with care for safety, and walk along Lake East and Lake West near the town center. The Lomé Convention was signed there in 1975."}

{"digest":"Boucle du Baoulé National Park lies in western Mali, in Kayes and Koulikoro regions, and was set up in 1982. Visitors would find a very large protected area with desert and semi-desert landscapes, dry lightly wooded savannah, riverine forest and thorn scrub, but little large wildlife. The park is known for prehistoric rock art and tombs. It also supports critically endangered Western chimpanzees and many bird species, and is part of the UNESCO Boucle du Baoulé Biosphere Reserve."}

{"digest":"Nananom Mpow is a traditional sacred grove associated with the Fante people in Ghana, near Obidan, the Eminsa Ɔkye river, and Mankessim. It is described as dense, biodiverse woodland with two large ponds, Atsendu Pond and Nananom Pond, fed by local watercourses. The grove is linked in Akan tradition to Oburumankoma, Odapagyan, and Oson, the legendary founders of Fante settlement. It was regarded as a sacred place and its destruction in 1851 is noted as a major clash between Christianity and traditional religion."}

{"digest":"The Presidential Palace, informally called the Grey Palace, is the residence of the President of Mauritania in central Nouakchott. A visitor would see it as the city’s most prominent landmark, set in extensive gardens and grounds. It stands just northwest of the Lebanese International University, next to the former US embassy, and south of the Central Bank of Mauritania headquarters. The passage says it was built with assistance from China."}

{"digest":"Bolama is a city on Bolama Island in the Bijagos Islands of Guinea-Bissau. Visitors can see an array of decaying and crumbling colonial buildings, including remains from when Bolama was the capital of Guinea-Bissau. The island also has some good beaches, but reaching them from town may require walking for several kilometres or renting a bike or motorbike. The passage notes that the beaches are best visited at high tide."}

{"digest":"Chã das Caldeiras, the “Plateau of the Crater,” is the area inside the original crater that formed Fogo island. The villages of Portela and Bangaeria stretch along the main road through the crater. Visitors can walk around the villages, see agriculture in the rich volcanic soil, and find grapes, apples, pears, peaches and figs grown there. The passage also describes it as the base for climbing Pico de Fogo, with guided hikes, and mentions a fog-forest hike towards Mosteiros."}

{"digest":"Deserto de Viana is a sand desert in northwestern Boa Vista, Cape Verde, east of Rabil and Sal Rei and west of Bofarreira. It is crossed by “Route 66” and is described as having haunting white sand dunes. The desert itself is not protected, but it lies beside the Boa Esperança nature reserve, which includes Lagoa do Rabil and Praia de Atalanta. It is considered one of the seven natural wonders of Cape Verde."}

{"digest":"Idanre Forest Reserve is a nature reserve in Idanre local government area, Ondo State, in south-west Nigeria. It covers 561 square kilometres and is designated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. The reserve is lowland rainforest, ranging from 10 to 400 metres in altitude. The passage does not describe visitor activities, but identifies it as a protected forest reserve of significant size in the region."}

{"digest":"Fogo Natural Park is a protected area on Fogo Island in Cape Verde, covering 84.69 km2 across three municipalities. Visitors would see the active stratovolcano of Pico do Fogo, including its crater, crater rim, and the Monte Velha forests. The volcano is the highest point in Cape Verde and the only active volcano in the islands. The park is also an Important Bird Area, with species such as Fea's petrel, Boyd's shearwater, and Cape Verde swift, and it contains rare endemic plants found only on the crater rim."}

{"digest":"Katsina is a Local Government Area and the capital city of Katsina State in northwest Nigeria. A visitor can see Marusa Gate, built around the 15th century during the construction of the city walls, and Katsina City Gate, noted for the wall surrounding it and its seven gates, built about 900 years ago during King Murabus’s reign. The city also has Muhammadu Dikko Stadium, an all-seater venue for football and athletics, home to Katsina United, with a gymnasium and fitness club."}

{"digest":"Lagoas de Cufada Natural Park is a protected area in Guinea-Bissau, established in 2000 as the country’s first protected area. It is 890 km2 and the largest freshwater reserve in the country, classified as a Ramsar Site, a wetland of international importance. Visitors would go for wildlife viewing, with reported chimpanzees nesting in oil palms and other animals including hippopotamus, waterbuck, roan antelope, African buffalo, leopard, hyena, African dwarf crocodile, and about 250 bird species."}

{"digest":"Kabafita Forest Park is a forest park in The Gambia, established in 1954 and covering 243 hectares at about 38 metres above sea level. It is used for producing firewood through afforestation with fast-growing coniferous wood, and it also has mango plantations. Visitors would mainly see forested land and these plantations, and may observe birds such as Silver eagle, African tree falcon, golden cuckoo, large honey indicator, gray-breasted woodpecker, whistle-warbler, and African black-eared orioles."}

{"digest":"Ilhéu de Curral Velho and adjacent coast Important Bird Area is in southeastern Boa Vista, Cape Verde, and includes the islet of Ilhéu de Curral Velho and the deserted village area of Curral Velho. The islet is an unvegetated, heavily eroded rock in a protected nature reserve. On the mainland are sand dunes, a lagoon and an oasis with palms, acacias and Tamarix senegalensis. Visitors would see arid-zone habitat, nesting beaches for Hawksbill and Loggerhead turtles, and breeding birds including brown booby, magnificent frigatebird, Cape Verde shearwater and several mainland species. It is also a Ramsar wetland of international importance."}

{"digest":"Mindelo is on the island of São Vicente and is the cultural capital of Cape Verde. Visitors can walk a circuit from Praça Nova past the historic CV Telecom building, Alliance Francaise, the eagle monument, Torre de Belem, the fish market, Praça Independencia, the church, parliament, Mercado Municipal, and Palácio do Povo before returning to the square. The town also has bars and restaurants with traditional music, a harbour, a small beach, a port, and views back along the coast. Boats to Santo Antão leave from the harbour."}

{"digest":"Mampong is the administrative capital of Mampong Municipality in Ghana’s Ashanti region, with a population of about 117,000 in 2021. It is located in a mountainous zone. Visitors would mainly see an educational centre, with institutions including the University of Winneba College of Agriculture, Mampong Technical College of Education, St Monica’s College of Education, and Mampong Nursing and Midwifery Training College, along with several secondary and basic schools. The community is headed by the Mamponghene, who holds a major chieftaincy title in the Ashanti kingdom."}

{"digest":"Langue de Barbarie National Park lies south of Saint-Louis in northern Senegal, about 18 km from the city. It combines mangroves, sand dunes, the Senegal River, tidal wetlands, beach and ocean. Visitors can see crabs, lizards, monkeys and more than 160 bird species, and watch birdlife on the park’s reproduction island. The park was established in 1976 to protect sea turtle nesting sites and is an important migratory bird sanctuary on the European bird migration route."}

{"digest":"Sungbo's Eredo is a system of defensive walls and ditches southwest of Ijebu Ode in Ogun State, Nigeria. The fortifications stretch for more than 160 kilometres and form an uneven ring around part of the ancient Ijebu Kingdom. Visitors would see a deep ditch with smooth walls, an inner bank, and walls flanked by trees and other vegetation, creating a green tunnel. It was built in honour of Oloye Bilikisu Sungbo and is on Nigeria's tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage Sites."}

{"digest":"Naa Gbewaa Shrine is a sacred ancestral shrine in Pusiga, in Ghana’s Upper East Region. It is dedicated to Naa Gbewaa, remembered as the founder of the Mamprusi, Dagomba, Nanumba, and related northern Ghanaian kingdoms. Visitors would see a site used for ancestral veneration, rituals, and communal gatherings, with access regulated and ceremonies carried out according to custom. Oral tradition places its establishment in the 14th century, and it is regarded as the resting place of Naa Gbewaa’s spirit."}

{"digest":"Santiago is an island of Cape Verde. Visitors can see Praia, the capital, and Cidade Velha, the former capital, where the historical and cultural sights are concentrated, with notable ruins. Tarrafal has an accessible swimming sand beach, hotels, nearby adventure sports, and the former dictatorial prison. The island also has Serra Malagueta National Park for hikes, steep mountain roads, east coast cliffs, black beaches, fishing ports, and beaches such as Praia da Prata and Aguas Belas. Travel is shaped by dry, mountainous scenery and sparse shared transport in smaller towns."}

{"digest":"Arly-Singou is a 6,388 km2 ecosystem in Burkina Faso that includes Arli National Park and the Singou Reserve. Visitors would be in one of the most important remaining savanna woodland wildlife areas in West Africa, where aerial surveys recorded elephants, buffalo, antelope, lions, warthog, baboons and patas monkeys. The passage says it once held the region’s largest antelope population and that antelope numbers have been sustained. It is also noted for a wildlife management project involving government funding and private operators."}

{"digest":"Bontioli Reserve is a wildlife sanctuary in Bougouriba Province, Sud-Ouest Region, Burkina Faso. Established in 1957, it covers 127 km2 and lies at 262 meters above sea level. A visitor would be in a protected reserve known for high biodiversity. The passage says it is one of three complete reserves in Burkina Faso and one of the country’s wildlife sanctuaries."}

{"digest":"The Tanbi Wetland Complex is a wetland reserve outside Banjul, at the mouth of the Gambia River. It covers about 6,000 hectares, mostly mangrove forest, with tidal creeks, lagoons, saline mudflats, and areas of saltmarsh and dry woodland. Visitors would see mangroves, occasional baobab and palm trees, and wildlife such as western red colobus monkeys, West African manatees, crocodiles, otters, and many birds. It was declared a Ramsar site and is important for flood control, erosion control, and sediment retention."}

{"digest":"Fort Winneba is a slave fort built by the Royal African Company in 1694 on the Gold Coast, in present-day Ghana. It was designed to support the trade in enslaved people. A 1727 survey by William Smith describes the fort as standing on rising ground near the seashore, with a tank supplying fresh water, an avenue of trees to the outer gate, a large spur, cattle secured at night, and good gardens. He said the place was pleasant and comfortable enough."}

{"digest":"Baía do Inferno is a bay on the southwest coast of Santiago in Cape Verde, within the municipality of Santa Catarina. Visitors would see a large, relatively sheltered bay bordered by steep cliffs that rise to more than 400 metres in places. It lies near Entre Picos de Reda inland, with Rincão and Porto Mosquito along the coast. The area is significant as part of an Important Bird Area: its cliffs support breeding red-billed tropicbirds and the largest colony of brown booby in Cape Verde."}

{"digest":"Curral Velho Protected Countryside is a protected landscape around a deserted village in southern Boa Vista, Cape Verde, about 25 km southeast of Sal Rei. A visitor would see the old houses of Curral Velho, São Domingos and Prazeres, which are examples of traditional Capeverdean architecture, though they are in poor condition. The nearby islet Ilhéu de Curral Velho and the adjacent coast are important for birds. The protected area covers 16.35 square kilometres."}

{"digest":"Wechiau Community Hippo Sanctuary is a community-based project protecting a 40km stretch of the Black Volta River in Ghana’s Upper West Region. The river supports one of the two remaining hippopotamus populations in Ghana. Visitors can view wildlife and take part in local Wala and Birifor (Lobi) tribal life and customs, with lodging and directions also provided. Created as a sanctuary by local chiefs in 1999, it is described as an eco-travel experience and received the Ghana Tourist Board’s Tourist Initiative of the Year Award in 2000."}

{"digest":"The Virtual Museum of Modern Nigerian Art is a website launched by Pan-Atlantic University in Lagos. It presents over 400 works by 81 artists, including pioneering Nigerian artists Aina Onabolu and Bruce Onobrakpeya, as well as emerging artists such as Richardson Ovbiebo and Babalola Lawson. The museum was created by Jess Castellote, a Spanish architect. Its significance in the passage is that it is part of Pan-Atlantic University’s wider expansion, alongside the later opening of the Yemisi Shyllon Museum of Art."}

{"digest":"Cacheu River Mangroves Natural Park is a national park on the Cacheu River in Guinea-Bissau. Visitors would see vast mangrove landscapes, with 68% of the park covered by mangroves, and a habitat that supports marine life, diverse flora and fauna, and large numbers of migratory birds that winter there. It is the largest compact mangrove environment in West Africa and has been a Ramsar site since 2015."}

{"digest":"Azougui, also called Azuggi, was a town on the Adrar Plateau in north-western Mauritania, north-west of Atar. In the eleventh century it was the first capital of the Almoravid dynasty and an important stop on the trans-Saharan trade route between Morocco and Ghana. Visitors can see surviving parts of the citadel and the necropolis of al-Imam al-Hadrami, as well as seventh-century rock carvings. The nearby site of Tabfarilla was where the Almoravids suffered an early defeat."}

{"digest":"Tamou Total Reserve is a nature and wildlife reserve in southwest Niger, in the Tillaberi Region. It covers about 756 km2 and lies next to W du Niger, as part of the larger W National Park and Transborder Reserve. Visitors would be in an area where local people also live and where the main focus is protecting African elephant populations that migrate through the region."}

{"digest":"Birimi is an archaeological site in northern Ghana, on the Gambaga escarpment about 3.5 kilometers northwest of Nalerigu, between Gambaga and Nalerigu. Visitors would not see a built monument but an excavated landscape with seasonal stream channels covered in lithic artifacts, and evidence of digging and research. The site has occupation phases from the Middle Stone Age, Later Stone Age, and Iron Age. It is significant for its Kintampo Complex remains, including pottery, wattle and daub structures, and charred plant remains showing pearl millet cultivation."}

{"digest":"The Royal Palaces of Abomey are 10 palaces in central Abomey, Benin, in the former capital of the Kingdom of Dahomey. Built by the kingdom’s rulers between 1695 and 1900, they once formed the cultural hub of the kingdom and could accommodate up to 8,000 people. Today they are no longer inhabited, and the palaces of King Ghézo and King Glélé house the Historical Museum of Abomey, which explains the kingdom’s history, symbolism, independence, resistance, and fight against colonial occupation. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site."}

{"digest":"Kokorou, also called Kokoro, is a town and rural commune in western Niger’s Téra Department. A visitor would see the nearby Kokoro and Namga Wetlands, a large shallow brackish basin in an ancient valley with sand dunes, granite outcrops and flat-topped hills around it. The wetlands hold water for much of the year, support migratory birds on the African-Eurasian flyway, and are used locally for supervised grazing and fishing for lungfish. The passage says the area is ecologically important and a Ramsar site."}

{"digest":"Badiar National Park is a national park in Guinea on the border with Senegal, contiguous with Senegal’s Niokolo-Koba National Park. It was established in 1985 partly in response to concerns about poaching. The park has two main sectors, Mafou and Kouya, plus a buffer zone around Mafou. Visitors would see savanna, open woodland, gallery forest, scrub woodland, wooded savanna and open forest, along with rivers such as the Koulountou and Mitji. It is an important ecosystem, a core area of the Badiar Biosphere Reserve and an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Katsina State is in North West Nigeria and was created from Kaduna State in 1987. Visitors can see the Emir of Katsina and Emir of Daura’s palaces, and visit Mai’Adua’s large historical market, which operates on Sundays. The city of Katsina and Daura are described as ancient seats of Islamic culture and learning. The state also hosts the Gani Festival in Daura, with a durbar, drumming, dancing, horsemanship, costumes, and historical artifacts, and the Kalankuwa youth festival with drama, wrestling, boxing, singing, and dancing."}

{"digest":"Burutu is a Local Government Area in Delta State, with its headquarters in Burutu town and the Atlantic Ocean to the south. A visitor would be in an area bordered by Ughelli South, Ethiope West, Ethiope East, Patani, Bayelsa State, and Rivers State. The people are mainly Ijaw, with some Urhobo and Itsekiri, and the main activities are fishing, agriculture, oil and gas. The passage also notes Forçados, which served as an administrative headquarters during the colonial era and hosted the Portuguese."}

{"digest":"Unubi is a rural area in Nnewi South Local Government, Anambra State, in southeastern Nigeria. It is one of the Igbo-speaking communities and has three main villages: Etitinabo, Nkwukwo and Isimba, with Isimba later divided into Isiokwe, Agbogwugwu and Akwueke, now called Akwuchukwu. A visitor would see a farming community producing yam, cassava, plantain, maize and fruits. The New Yam Festival, or Iri Ji, is its most prominent event, marked by blessing the new yams, feasting, dancing and communal prayers."}

{"digest":"Arch 22 is a commemorative arch on the road into Banjul, on the Banjul-Serrekunda Highway. Built in 1996, it marks the military coup of 22 July 1994 that overthrew President Sir Dawda Jawara’s elected government. The 35-metre structure has eight columns and three floors. Visitors can go up by elevator or spiral stairs to a second-floor gallery with views over Banjul, the sea port, and the Tanbi Wetland Complex, and a top-floor textile museum. A statue of an unknown soldier stands near the base."}

{"digest":"Esie is an Igbomina Yoruba town in Kwara State, North Central Nigeria, about 48 km south east of Ilorin. A visitor would see the town itself and its well-known collection of about 800 soapstone figures, for which Esie is generally known. The passage also says the town was founded by Prince Baragbon around 1770. Esie has a king, Oba Yakubu Babalola Egunjobi II, and the Yoruba dialect spoken there is predominantly Igbonna."}

{"digest":"Lake Higa is a small lake in eastern Burkina Faso, near the border with Niger. It covers 228 hectares and lies at an elevation of 271 metres. The lake drains into the Babangou, which in turn drains into the Niger. The passage gives no visitor activities, but it notes the site around Lake Higa was included in the Ramsar List of wetlands of international importance in 2009."}

{"digest":"Ajegunle is a town in Lagos State, in the Ajeromi-Ifelodun local government area of southwest Nigeria. A visitor would find a large, densely populated settlement with about 550,000 residents drawn from many of Nigeria’s ethnic groups. The passage says it is often seen as the slum or ghetto of Lagos State. Its name in Yoruba means “A place where riches dwell.”"}

{"digest":"The Inner Niger Delta, also called the Macina or Masina, is an inland river delta in central Mali, south of the Sahara. It is a 400 km-long area of wetlands, lakes, floodplains, and channels along the Niger and Bani rivers, with towns including Mopti, Sévaré, and Djenné, where the mud-brick Great Mosque stands. Visitors would see a landscape that changes with the seasons, with floodwater, fishing, agriculture, and many birds in the wet season. The area is inhabited by the Fulani and Dogon and has a history of empires and French conquest."}

{"digest":"Ogoja is a town and Local Government Area in Cross River State, South South Nigeria, on the A4 highway. Visitors would mainly see a town made up of many tribal units and communities, including Igoli, Ishibori, Mbube and Ekajuk, with several named villages. The area is mainly inhabited by the Ekoi peoples. The passage says its livelihood is subsistence agriculture, with farming of cassava, yams, palm oil and related crops. It was one of the provinces in pre-colonial times."}

{"digest":"Koumbi Saleh, also called Kumbi Saleh, is the site of ruined ancient and medieval city remains in southeast Mauritania, and it may have been the capital of the Ghana Empire. Visitors would see excavated ruins of a large Muslim town, including stone houses and a congregational mosque; the king’s town described in medieval sources has not been found. The site is significant for its possible link to the Ghana Empire and the trans-Saharan gold trade, with occupation dating from the late 5th to 14th centuries."}

{"digest":"Monument de la Paix in Bamako is described as a fitting monument with a dove perched atop a world held in an equilateral triangle. The passage also places it among several other Bamako sights, including the Muso Kunda Museum, Bamako Regional Museum, Bamako Zoo, the Bamako Botanical Gardens, the National Conference Center Tower, the Souvenir Pyramid, the Independence Monument, Al Quoods Monument, the Hamdallaye obelisk, the Modibo Keita Memorial, and Point G hill with caves containing rock paintings."}

{"digest":"Umuchu is one of the largest towns in Aguata Local Government Area of Anambra State, Nigeria, on the boundary between Anambra and Imo States. It is connected by road to Umunze in the east and Igbo-Ukwu in the northwest. The town is home to the Igbo people, and Igbo is also the local dialect. A visitor would see churches such as St. Mathew Catholic Church, St. Thomas Anglican Church, St. Peters Anglican Church, and Zion City Umuchu, along with Honeywell Hotel, a multipurpose computer centre, and Orient Mega 101.7FM. It is also noted for evolving from a decentralized structure to unified leadership with the first Igwe in South East Nigeria."}

{"digest":"Basse Casamance National Park, near Oussouye in Ziguinchor, is one of Senegal’s six national parks. Created in 1970, it covers 5,000 hectares of Guinean forest and savannah woodland. The passage says it is currently closed to visitors because of the Casamance conflict and possible land mines. Its wildlife includes about 200 bird species and 50 mammal species, among them African forest buffalo, African leopard, Campbell’s mona monkey, Prince Demidoff’s bushbaby and western red colobus."}

{"digest":"Museu dos Náufragos in Boavista, Cape Verde, is a private museum of anthropological and artistic interest. Visitors see a permanent exhibition of cultural anthropology, art, and underwater archaeology finds, organized around the history and culture of the Cape Verde islands, the universal language of art, and the journey of a “castaway” toward salvation. The building was made with materials found on the island, with attention to recycling. It also hosts temporary exhibitions and serves as a place for open discussion about identity and the future."}

{"digest":"The Centre for National Culture in Kumasi, Ashanti Region, is a cultural centre established in 1956 and formerly called the National Cultural Centre. It is the site of the Prempeh II Jubilee Museum. The centre was planned as an open-air museum to preserve and showcase Asante culture, with facilities including a library, traditional chapel, exhibition hall, theatre, dance arena, and museum. Visitors would see the museum and the centre’s main attraction, the Traditional House for the Ashanti Museum and Art Gallery. It was renamed in 1963 and again in 1990."}

{"digest":"Assinie, also called Assinie-Mafia, is a resort town in Côte d’Ivoire’s Lagunes region, at the mouth of the Aby Lagoon. Visitors can see the narrow peninsula of La Passe across from town, with luxury villas, high-rise resorts, and beaches. On the lagoon side, the setting is more traditional, with wooden and straw houses occupied by fishermen living between the lagoon and the sea. Much of this area is part of Îles Ehotilé National Park."}

{"digest":"Saboba is the administrative capital of Saboba District in northeastern Ghana, in the Volta Basin along the border with Togo. It is widely recognized as a major cultural headquarters for the Konkomba people. A visitor would see a district centre in a border setting rather than a tourism site described for specific attractions. The passage notes that the people of Saboba speak Likpakpaaln, with the Bichaabob as the majority accent."}

{"digest":"Lake Piso, also called Lake Pisu or Fisherman’s Lake, is an oblong tidal lagoon in Grand Cape Mount County near Robertsport in western Liberia. It is Liberia’s largest lake and is connected to the Atlantic Ocean by a narrow inlet. Visitors would see islands such as Massatin Island, with monkeys and birds, and may watch or take part in fishing and water sports including swimming, canoeing, and water skiing. The lake is an Important Bird Area and the Lake Piso wetlands were Liberia’s only designated wetland of international importance."}

{"digest":"The Independence Monument in Lomé, the capital of Togo, was built to honour the country’s independence from France. Visitors would see a white bust of a woman holding up a cooking pot before a silhouette of a figure with raised arms, as if breaking chains. The monument carries inscriptions celebrating Togo’s nationhood and the proclamation of independence on 27 April 1960. It is near the Palais des congrès de Lomé, which houses the Togo National Museum, and Paul Ahyi contributed to its design."}

{"digest":"Réserve naturelle de sel iodé is a small nature reserve in Nouakchott, Mauritania, formed from a sebkha, a semi-arid salted wetland. It lies on Avenue Gamal Abdel Nasser, near the Ministry of Energy headquarters and opposite the Centre neuro-psychiatrique de Nouakchott, north of the urban commune of Sebkha. The passage gives its significance mainly as a natural reserve and identifies its urban location."}

{"digest":"Andoni Elephant Park, also called Andoni Elephant Sanctuary, is a community forest on Andoni Island in the Niger Delta in Rivers State, Nigeria. A visitor would see a reserve made up of freshwater swamp forest, tidal flats with estuaries, mangroves and creeks, and Atlantic beach. The passage says the park was officially gazetted in 1983. It is described as one of the last remaining pristine natural resources on the island and as habitat for endemic or near-endemic mammals, including African forest elephant, pygmy hippopotamus, West African manatee, sitatunga and waterbuck."}

{"digest":"Lafiagi is a town in Kwara State, west central Nigeria, on the south bank of the Niger River. Founded in 1810 by Fulani leaders Malam Maliki and Manzuma as a fortified town in Nupe territory, it later became the seat of an emirate and then, in 1949, the title of its ruler changed from emir to chief. Today it is the headquarters of the Edun Local Government Council and a market centre for rice, yams, grains, fish, cattle, cotton, and other produce. Cotton weaving is traditionally important."}

{"digest":"B. Leza was Francisco Xavier da Cruz, a Cape Verdean writer, composer and singer of morna music, born in Mindelo on São Vicente. He innovated in the morna genre, used passing chords, and wrote poems that appeared in Claridade. His work gained success in the 1950s and influenced Cape Verdean music for the next twenty years. He composed many mornas, including Eclipse, Miss Perfumado, Resposta de Segredo Cu Mar and Lua Nha Testemunha."}

{"digest":"Guinee Forestiere is a forested region in southeast Guinea, covering all of Nzerekore province and home to several ethnic groups, including the Toma and Lissi. Visitors would see jungle landscape and Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve, a 116,200-hectare Biosphere Reserve. The reserve is described as a relict of the once continuous West African rainforest belt. The passage also mentions wild chimpanzees at I.R.E.B."}

{"digest":"Akungba Akoko is a town in Ondo State, southwest Nigeria, near Ikare-Akoko. It became widely known after Adekunle Ajasin University was established there in 1999, having previously been in Ado-Ekiti. Before the university, the town was unpopular and sparsely populated. Visitors would chiefly see the university, which the passage describes as having a beautiful landscape and a cool learning environment. The Akungba people have lived in the area for about a century and were once ruled by Owo."}

{"digest":"The Sankarani River is a tributary of the Niger River that rises in the Guinea Highlands of the Fouta Djallon. It flows north from Guinea into southern Mali, joining the Niger about 40 kilometres upstream of Bamako, and it also forms part of the Ivory Coast-Guinea and Guinea–Mali borders. Visitors would see a river with a discontinuous floodplain, gallery forests, the Sélingué Dam and reservoir, and fishing activity. The passage also says Niani, on its banks, was believed to be the capital of the ancient Mali Empire."}

{"digest":"Tiwai Island, meaning “Big Island” in Mende, is a 12-square-kilometre wildlife sanctuary and tourist site on the Moa River in Sierra Leone’s Southern Province. Visitors can see its tropical island landscape and wildlife, including pygmy hippopotamuses, more than 135 bird species, and a very high diversity of primates. The island has been used for ecological research, wildlife management, conservation, and tourism, and it was officially designated a game reserve in 1987. It was later designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Gola-Tiwai complex."}

{"digest":"Chiranci, also called Charanchi, is a town and local government headquarters in Katsina State, northern Nigeria. Visitors would see local markets, traditional crafts, and welcoming communities, and get a view of rural life. Hausa is widely spoken, with English used in official communication and by educated locals. The town is rich in Hausa-Fulani culture, language, and traditions, and Islam strongly shapes its customs and celebrations. Its history is linked to the ancient Hausa kingdoms and Islamic empires of the region."}

{"digest":"Ilhéu de Cima is an uninhabited island in Cape Verde, part of the Ilhéus do Rombo islet group and the Brava municipality. It lies east of Ilhéu Grande and northeast of Brava, within the integral nature reserve Ilhéus do Rombo, noted for seabird colonies. The island’s highest point is in the south, where the Ilhéu de Cima Lighthouse stands, the only building on the island. The passage also notes endemic fauna such as the Iago sparrow and a sponge species found in nearby deep waters."}

{"digest":"Abacha is a town in Idemili North Local Government Area of Anambra State, South East Nigeria. A visitor would see a community known for Igbo culture, history, festivals, traders, and local leadership under an Igwe, supported by village councils, age-grade groups, and elders. The town has five recognised villages, including Umudisi and Umuazu. Its most prominent event is the annual New Yam Festival, when the Igwe or elders bless new yams before they are eaten, marking the start of yam harvest."}

{"digest":"Fort Batenstein was a Dutch fort and trading post near Butre on the Gold Coast, built in 1656 on a hill overlooking Butre Bay. Visitors would see the site of a former fort associated with the signing of the Treaty of Butre in 1656, a sawmill added in the 18th century, and the place where the Dutch later concentrated military effort during the Dutch–Ahanta War in 1837. It was ceded to Britain in 1872 and designated a World Heritage Site in 1979 for its historical importance in European trade and exploitation in West Africa."}

{"digest":"Praia is Cape Verde’s capital and busiest city, on the southern end of Santiago Island. Visitors would see a large urban area spread across a plateau overlooking the bay, with the city center at the Platô, residential districts, a bazaar area called Sucupira, and the port and airport nearby. The passage says the city is mainly residential, but worth a half-day exploration when passing through. Praia is significant as the home of about one in four Cape Verdeans, and its port handles agricultural products and seafood."}

{"digest":"Orango is the largest island in the Bijagós Islands, about 60 kilometres off mainland Guinea-Bissau. Its largest village is Eticoga, and it forms part of Orango National Park with nearby islands. Visitors would know it for its saltwater hippopotamuses and for the traditions of its inhabitants. The passage says women formally propose marriage by offering specially prepared fish, and the bride-to-be later builds the home herself. Orango was also the seat of Okinka Pampa until her death in 1930."}

{"digest":"Singou Reserve is a protected area in Gourma Province, Burkina Faso, established in 1955 and covering 1,926 km2. It is the country’s largest reserve by surface area and one of three complete reserves in Burkina Faso. The passage does not describe visitor activities inside the reserve, but it says Singou is part of a protected-area complex with Arli National Park. Together, they form an important bird area."}

{"digest":"Upper East Region is in northern Ghana, in the Ghanaian Northern Plains, and is the country’s third smallest region. Visitors would see a landscape of gentle slopes, rock outcrops, uplands, and the Gambaga Scarp, with sparse savanna trees such as baobabs, acacias, and shea. Places named in the passage include Sirigu, described as a scenic village, and the Tongo Hills, a granite mountain range. Its capital, Bolgatanga, is a center for woven baskets, leather goods, and straw handicrafts. The region is noted for its cultural heritage and historical significance."}

{"digest":"Bafing National Park is a protected area in southern Mali covering 5,000 km2. The landscape is mainly woodland. It is the only protected area for chimpanzees in the Manding Plateau area. Visitors would see a park noted for its birdlife, including violet turacos, blue-bellied rollers, fox kestrels, Senegal parrots, bronze-tailed starlings, white-crowned robin-chats, white-fronted black-chats, Mali and black-faced firefinches, and grey-headed olivebacks. It is part of the Bafing Biosphere and has been designated an Important Bird Area."}

{"digest":"Fort Victoria is a fort in western Cape Coast, Ghana, first called Phipps Tower after Governor Phipps and later renamed for Queen Victoria. Built in 1821 on the site of an earlier fort, it served as an outlook post for signaling and for fending off attacks. It is in good condition, maintained as a national monument, and can be viewed from Fort William. Along with nearby forts and castles, it was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1979 for its European colonial significance."}

{"digest":"Sahelian Mauritania is a semi-arid region in southern Mauritania, extending to the Senegal River Valley on the borders with Senegal and Mali. Visitors can see Tichit, a village near a UNESCO site with some of the oldest stone buildings in Africa south of the Sahara, and Oualata, a small oasis town that is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site.
